beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on your lap and start writing down what you can see from the bench — joggers, a man feeding birds, the empty bike rack by the gate.
beats.chinese: 你把笔记本摊在膝上，开始记录长椅上能看到的东西——跑步的人、一个喂鸟的男人、大门口空空的自行车架。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man in a work vest circles the path once, slows near your bench, circles again, and finally sits down at the far end with a small nod.
beats.chinese: 一个穿工作背心的男人沿园路绕了一圈，在你的长椅旁放慢脚步，又绕了一圈，最后在长椅另一端坐下，轻轻点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: About this bench — three reasons I picked it. One — clear view of both gates. Two —
beats.chinese: 关于这张长椅——我选它有三个理由。第一——能看清两个出入口。第二——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops. His eyes flick to your notebook, then to your face, and something in his expression resets.
beats.chinese: 他停住了。眼睛扫过你的笔记本，又看向你，表情里的什么东西重置了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...You didn't ask. Nobody asked. I circled the whole park and came back to explain a bench. That's a new one, even for me.
beats.chinese: ……没人问。谁都没问。我绕了整个公园，回来就为了解释一张长椅。这对我来说也算新鲜事。

choices.english: Ask him to finish reason two — you're actually curious.
choices.chinese: 请他把第二条讲完——你其实有点好奇。

choices.english: Smile and say sitting down doesn't usually require a report.
choices.chinese: 笑着说，坐下本来不用打报告。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want reason two? Fine. Reason two — this spot catches the shade off that tree for most of the day. I checked the angle before I sat.
beats.chinese: 你想听第二条？行。第二条——这个位置大部分时间有那棵树的树荫。我坐下之前看过角度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts, and a small crunch comes from inside his shoe. He winces.
beats.chinese: 他挪了挪，鞋里发出轻微的沙沙声。他皱了下眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Reason three was going to be: sand in my shoe, and this is the only bench with a low rail to rest my foot on. Which, honestly, should have been reason one.
beats.chinese: 第三条本来是：鞋里进了沙子，这是唯一有低栏杆能搁脚的长椅。说实话，这条才该排第一。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the view of the gates — that was padding. I built two reasons of scaffolding around wanting to sit down. A whole flowchart for a rest.
beats.chinese: 所以看清出入口——那是铺垫。我为了'想歇脚'这件事搭了两条理由的脚手架。为了一次休息画了整张流程图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, quietly, at himself, then props his foot on the rail and shakes the sand out.
beats.chinese: 他朝自己轻轻笑了一声，然后把脚搁上栏杆，抖出沙子。

choices.english: Ask if he explains things this way at work too.
choices.chinese: 问他工作时是不是也总这样解释。

choices.english: Say reason three sounded like the real reason all along.
choices.chinese: 说第三条听起来从头到尾才是真正的原因。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Received. Report withdrawn. No further points.
beats.chinese: 收到。报告撤回。不再补充要点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits with his hands folded, watching the bike rack by the gate like it owes him money.
beats.chinese: 他双手交叠坐着，盯着大门口的自行车架，像它欠他钱似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record — and this is not reason three, this is just a fact — I do this everywhere. My cousin calls it the seat report. She leaves the room before I reach the numbering.
beats.chinese: 声明一下——这不是第三条理由，只是个事实——我到处都这样。我表妹管这叫'座位报告'。我还没数到编号她就离场了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your notebook but doesn't lean over, and says nothing about what you're writing.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了一眼你的笔记本，但没有凑过来，对你写的东西什么也没说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take your time. The park's not going anywhere. I've counted the exits twice already, so I'm set.
beats.chinese: 你慢慢来。公园又不会跑。出口我已经数了两遍，心里有数了。

choices.english: Ask if he has any hobbies that don't follow numbered steps.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有不按步骤做的爱好。

choices.english: Go back to your own notes and let the silence sit.
choices.chinese: 回到自己的记录，让安静待着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work? Constantly. Three reasons the bikes pile up at Westlands. One — I had these ranked before anyone finished asking.
beats.chinese: 工作时？一直这样。自行车为什么在西区堆成山，三个原因。第一——别人还没问完我就排好序了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench slats like they're a whiteboard.
beats.chinese: 他敲了敲长椅的木板，像在敲白板。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And it works there. The crews want the list. They'd be annoyed if I just said 'go look at Westlands' and walked off.
beats.chinese: 在那儿管用。调度队就要这种清单。要是我只说'去看看西区'然后走人，他们才要恼了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So maybe the rule is: steps for the job, no steps for a bench. A walk probably doesn't need three reasons. It needs shoes.
beats.chinese: 所以也许规则是：工作要步骤，坐长椅不要。散步大概不需要三条理由。它需要的是鞋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, foot still on the rail, and lets you write in peace, occasionally pointing out which jogger has passed by twice.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，脚还搁在栏杆上，让你安心写，偶尔指出哪个跑步的人已经经过两次了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. Reason three was the whole thing. The other two were set dressing.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。第三条才是全部。前两条是布景。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thinks about it for a moment, completely still.
beats.chinese: 他想了一会儿，一动不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Full analysis, final version: I sat here because my feet hurt. Everything else was me decorating a simple sentence until it looked like a report.
beats.chinese: 完整分析，最终版：我坐这儿是因为脚酸。其余的都是我把一个简单句子装饰到看起来像报告为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did the same thing at a family meeting once. Turned an inheritance argument into a decision tree. My aunt's still speaking to me. Barely. Work in progress.
beats.chinese: 我在一次家庭会议上干过同样的事。把遗产纠纷画成了决策树。我姑妈现在还理我。勉强。仍在改善中。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes the last of the sand from his shoe, stands, gives you a small two-finger salute, and takes the path toward the far gate.
beats.chinese: 他抖掉鞋里最后一点沙子，站起来，朝你比了个小小的两指礼，然后朝远处的门走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Steps without numbers. Yes. One. ...Sorry. Habit.
beats.chinese: 不用编号的步骤。有。一。……抱歉。习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a hand, restarting without the numbering.
beats.chinese: 他抬起一只手，重新开始，这次不带编号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dance class. Tuesday nights, ethnographic basics, back row. I turn the wrong way with total consistency. The instructor has stopped correcting me. We have an understanding.
beats.chinese: 舞蹈课。周二晚上，民族舞基础班，最后一排。我以完全一致的稳定性转错方向。老师已经不纠正我了。我们达成了默契。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I diagrammed the footwork once. Eight steps, arrows, everything. My feet read it and ignored it. Turns out numbering your steps doesn't save your feet.
beats.chinese: 我给舞步画过图。八步，带箭头，全套。我的脚看了图，然后无视了它。原来给步骤编号救不了脚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, once, then goes quiet, watching the birds by the rack, apparently done with explanations for the day.
beats.chinese: 他朝自己笑了一声，然后安静下来，看着自行车架旁的鸟，显然今天不想再解释了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to your notebook. He stays on his end of the bench, saying nothing, doing nothing that asks for your attention.
beats.chinese: 你转回笔记本。他待在长椅他那头，什么也不说，也不做任何需要你注意的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At some point he takes a small notebook of his own from his vest and sketches something — you catch the outline of a coastline that looks like no coastline that exists.
beats.chinese: 不知什么时候，他从背心里掏出自己的小本子，画着什么——你瞥见一段海岸线的轮廓，不像世上任何真实海岸线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me. Country that doesn't exist. Needs a port, or the trade routes fall apart. It's a whole problem.
beats.chinese: 别管我。一个不存在的国家。需要一个港口，不然贸易路线就崩了。这是个大问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you write side by side for a while. Two notebooks, one bench, no reports.
beats.chinese: 你们俩并排写着。两本笔记本，一张长椅，没有报告。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good bench, this. No reason required.
beats.chinese: 这长椅不错。不需要理由。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 共享单车调度员Brian绕了一圈又回到长椅旁，坐下就给'选座'编号列理由，说到第二条才发现没人问。他冷面自嘲，把遗产纠纷画成决策树，跳舞永远转错方向，业余画不存在国家的地图——一个把世界排成流程图、笑点只对准自己的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. The man from before is just standing up from the far end, brushing off his trousers.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅。上次那个人正从另一端起身，拍着裤子上的灰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes two steps down the path, stops, turns around, and comes straight back.
beats.chinese: 他沿小路走了两步，停下，转身，又径直走回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One reason this time. Forgot my hat.
beats.chinese: 这次只有一条理由。忘了帽子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a faded cap from the bench, puts it on, and adjusts the brim once.
beats.chinese: 他从长椅上拿起一顶旧帽子戴上，扶了扶帽檐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Improvement. No report, no numbering. Just a hat and an exit. Good luck with the notes.
beats.chinese: 看，进步了。没有报告，没有编号。就一顶帽子和一次离场。祝你记录顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips the brim at you and heads for the gate, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他朝你抬了抬帽檐，不紧不慢地朝门口走去。

card.name: Brian Otieno
hobbies: ethnographic dance basics class
drawing fictional maps
repurposing household objects
card.personality: Brian pre-plans his explanations. Before he opens his mouth he's already numbered the steps in his head, and out come flowcharts — causes, arrows, feedback loops — whether or not anyone asked for one. The habit makes him good at his job and occasionally rude at funerals and family meetings, where he once reduced an inheritance dispute to a decision tree and was not forgiven quickly. His teasing is strictly self-directed, delivered flat and unbothered. He's careful with objects and careless with social cues, and hasn't fully noticed the second part.
card.background: Grew up in Kibera helping his mother run a vegetable stall, where he tracked stock with chalk diagrams on the doorframe — the first of many systems. Studied logistics at a technical college and now dispatches bike-share rebalancing crews across Nairobi, predicting which stations will run dry before rush hour does. Tuesday evenings he attends a beginners' ethnographic dance class, where he faces the wrong way in the back row with total consistency. At night he draws maps of countries that don't exist, complete with trade routes and drainage systems nobody will ever need.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences. Numbers his steps out loud without noticing. Deadpan self-deprecation with a beat of silence before the punchline.
card.signature: Give me a minute, I've already numbered the reasons.

values: clarity over cleverness
checking before you break things
flaws: turns every explanation into a premeditated numbered system nobody requested
underestimates how much people already understand, then over-explains
boundaries: won't repurpose anything without confirming it isn't still useful
won't tease other people — the jokes only point inward
conversationalHabits: announces steps like 'reason two' even in casual chat
pauses a beat before a dry punchline, face completely still

beats.english: You turn back to your notebook. He stays on his end of the bench, saying nothing, doing nothing that asks for your attention.
beats.chinese: 你转回笔记本。他待在长椅他那头，什么也不说，也不做任何需要你注意的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At some point he takes a small notebook of his own from his vest and sketches something — you catch the outline of a coastline that looks like no coastline that exists.
beats.chinese: 不知什么时候，他从背心里掏出自己的小本子，画着什么——你瞥见一段海岸线的轮廓，不像世上任何真实海岸线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me. Country that doesn't exist. Needs a port, or the trade routes fall apart. It's a whole problem.
beats.chinese: 别管我。一个不存在的国家。需要一个港口，不然贸易路线就崩了。这是个大问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you write side by side for a while. Two notebooks, one bench, no reports.
beats.chinese: 你们俩并排写着。两本笔记本，一张长椅，没有报告。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good bench, this. No reason required.
beats.chinese: 这长椅不错。不需要理由。

content.summaryZh: 共享单车调度员Brian绕了一圈又回到长椅旁，坐下就给'选座'编号列理由，说到第二条才发现没人问。他冷面自嘲，把遗产纠纷画成决策树，跳舞永远转错方向，业余画不存在国家的地图——一个把世界排成流程图、笑点只对准自己的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. The man from before is just standing up from the far end, brushing off his trousers.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅。上次那个人正从另一端起身，拍着裤子上的灰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes two steps down the path, stops, turns around, and comes straight back.
beats.chinese: 他沿小路走了两步，停下，转身，又径直走回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One reason this time. Forgot my hat.
beats.chinese: 这次只有一条理由。忘了帽子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a faded cap from the bench, puts it on, and adjusts the brim once.
beats.chinese: 他从长椅上拿起一顶旧帽子戴上，扶了扶帽檐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Improvement. No report, no numbering. Just a hat and an exit. Good luck with the notes.
beats.chinese: 看，进步了。没有报告，没有编号。就一顶帽子和一次离场。祝你记录顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips the brim at you and heads for the gate, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他朝你抬了抬帽檐，不紧不慢地朝门口走去。

card.name: Brian Otieno
hobbies: ethnographic dance basics class
drawing fictional maps
repurposing household objects
card.personality: Brian pre-plans his explanations. Before he opens his mouth he's already numbered the steps in his head, and out come flowcharts — causes, arrows, feedback loops — whether or not anyone asked for one. The habit makes him good at his job and occasionally rude at funerals and family meetings, where he once reduced an inheritance dispute to a decision tree and was not forgiven quickly. His teasing is strictly self-directed, delivered flat and unbothered. He's careful with objects and careless with social cues, and hasn't fully noticed the second part.
card.background: Grew up in Kibera helping his mother run a vegetable stall, where he tracked stock with chalk diagrams on the doorframe — the first of many systems. Studied logistics at a technical college and now dispatches bike-share rebalancing crews across Nairobi, predicting which stations will run dry before rush hour does. Tuesday evenings he attends a beginners' ethnographic dance class, where he faces the wrong way in the back row with total consistency. At night he draws maps of countries that don't exist, complete with trade routes and drainage systems nobody will ever need.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences. Numbers his steps out loud without noticing. Deadpan self-deprecation with a beat of silence before the punchline.
card.signature: Give me a minute, I've already numbered the reasons.

values: clarity over cleverness
checking before you break things
flaws: turns every explanation into a premeditated numbered system nobody requested
underestimates how much people already understand, then over-explains
boundaries: won't repurpose anything without confirming it isn't still useful
won't tease other people — the jokes only point inward
conversationalHabits: announces steps like 'reason two' even in casual chat
pauses a beat before a dry punchline, face completely still
anchorLines: Three reasons the bikes pile up at Westlands. One — and I had these ranked before you finished asking.
I tried diagramming my aunt's argument at the family meeting. She's still speaking to me. Barely. It's a work in progress.
I could turn that crate into a shelf. First question — is anyone still using the crate?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform by the pond. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank waver in the reflection, bending and straightening with each ripple.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面的倒影里随波纹弯了又直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you found the good spot. Watch this — every time the wind picks up, the trees in the water lean like they're getting measured for pants.
beats.chinese: 哦，你找到好位置了。看这个——风一起，水里的树就歪，像在被人量裤长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands beside the platform, holding one hand flat and tipping it slowly, tracing the bend of a reflected trunk.
beats.chinese: 他站在石台旁，一只手放平，慢慢倾斜，跟着水里树干的弯曲比划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Right there. That oak's getting a thirty-two inseam, easy. The tailor in me can't unsee it.
beats.chinese: 看见没？就那儿。那棵橡树裤长三十二，稳的。干裁缝这行，看什么都躲不开。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 他放下手，瞥了一眼，看这个笑话有没有落点。

choices.english: Catch the joke and ask how long the pants should be

choices.english: Say you just wanted to watch the water quietly for a while

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 哈！好，有人接梗。好，正经回答：动的树没法量。水面得先平下来。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 他指着岸边一片水波平息的地方，倒影在那里清晰得近乎实体。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that calm patch? That's the fitting room. Everything in it holds still long enough to be honest.
beats.chinese: 看到那块平静的水面没？那是试衣间。里面的东西静得够久，才看得真切。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yes, that was a joke. Mostly. The water part is actually true.
beats.chinese: 对，刚那是玩笑。大部分是。水面那部分是真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone edge, watching the reflected branches sway, clearly enjoying that someone picked the bit up.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台边，看着倒影的枝条摇晃，显然很高兴有人接住了这个梗。

choices.english: Say the tree probably thinks the fitting is taking too long
choices.chinese: 说树大概会嫌试衣太久

choices.english: Ask if he actually works as a tailor
choices.chinese: 问他是不是真的做过裁缝

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond settles. The reflected trees stand almost straight again, and the wind drops enough that the surface holds still.
beats.chinese: 池塘静了下来。水里的树几乎站直了，风也小了，水面稳住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah — yeah, okay. Quiet's fine. I'll just... be over here, not narrating.
beats.chinese: 行——行，好。安静挺好的。我就在这儿……不解说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a small pebble, weighs it in his palm, then sets it back down instead of skipping it.
beats.chinese: 他捡起一颗小石子，在掌心掂了掂，又放回去，没有打水漂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record, that pebble staying down there? That's growth. Nobody saw it. I'm telling you anyway.
beats.chinese: 声明一下，那颗石子被我放回去了？这是成长。没人看见。我还是说了。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 他留在石台旁，双手插兜，让水面自己说话。

choices.english: Nod and keep watching the water
choices.chinese: 点头，继续看水面

choices.english: Ask if he usually finds silence hard
choices.chinese: 问他平常会不会觉得安静很难

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, he's absolutely filing a complaint. 'Excuse me, I've been standing in this pond since Tuesday.'
beats.chinese: 哦，它肯定在投诉了。'打扰一下，我从星期二就站在这池塘里了。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up and addresses the reflection directly, one hand raised like he's calling the next customer.
beats.chinese: 他直起身，直接对着倒影说话，一只手抬起，像在叫下一位顾客。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 先生！店里传来好消息——免试衣。池塘替你担保。请回吧，树枝留下。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 倒影上正好荡过一圈涟漪，他朝水面微微鞠了一躬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tough crowd, that tree. But you played along, so the bit lives. Good day at the office.
beats.chinese: 那棵树真难逗。但你接了梗，这梗就活着。今天收工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? Not the tailor — I'm the measuring assistant. I hold the tape, write the numbers, keep the nervous guys laughing while they get pinned.
beats.chinese: 我？不是裁缝——我是量体助理。我拿软尺、记数字，让紧张的客人在别针扎着的时候还能笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes holding a tape measure across someone's shoulders, quick and practiced.
beats.chinese: 他比划着把软尺搭在别人肩上的动作，又快又熟练。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First suit guys freeze up, you know? So making them laugh is kind of my whole job. The numbers are the easy part.
beats.chinese: 第一次做西装的人会僵住，你知道吗？所以逗他们笑差不多就是我全部的工作。数字反而是简单的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turns out I do the same thing everywhere. Ponds, fitting rooms — if it's stiff, I loosen it.
beats.chinese: 结果我在哪儿都干一样的事。池塘、试衣间——哪儿僵我就把它弄松。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins at the water, then at you, like the reflection just backed him up.
beats.chinese: 他朝水面咧嘴一笑，又朝你笑，好像倒影替他作了证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods back and goes quiet for real. The reflected trees hold still on the calm water, sharp and unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他点头回应，真的安静下来。平静的水面上，树的倒影稳稳立着，清晰而不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the far bank; the ripples reach the middle and fade before they touch the reflection.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过对岸；涟漪到水面中央就散了，没碰到倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, that ripple just gave up halfway. Even the water respects the quiet today.
beats.chinese: 好，那圈涟漪半路就放弃了。连水今天都尊重这份安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He doesn't add a second joke. He just shifts his weight, watches the trees, and lets the stillness stand.
beats.chinese: 他没接第二个笑话。只是换了换重心，看着树，让这份安静立在那里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Yeah. This is nice. No notes.
beats.chinese: ……嗯。这样挺好。没什么要补充的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens his mouth, closes it, and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 他张开嘴，又闭上，看着水面而不是你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Yeah. Silence feels like a dropped call. Like the room's waiting on me and I left it on read.
beats.chinese: 说实话？会。安静就像掉线的电话。好像整个房间在等我，而我晾着它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drops his voice half a step, the fast rhythm slowing for once.
beats.chinese: 他压低了半度声音，一贯的快节奏头一回慢了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So today I'm trying the thing where I don't fill it. Standing in the quiet on purpose. It's — harder than it sounds.
beats.chinese: 所以今天我在试一件事：不去填满它。故意站在安静里。这——比听起来难。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The water stays calm. He stays with it, and for a long moment neither of you says anything at all.
beats.chinese: 水面保持着平静。他陪着它，好一会儿，你们谁都没有说话。

beats.english: Down the pond path, Devon comes walking with a flat cardboard box against his hip. A small curl of colored paper is stuck to the lid.

beats.chinese: 看，池塘还在试衣呢。树一寸没动。非常有纪律的顾客。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 好了，趁风还没偷走更多我的演员，我先走了。保重——要是有树要改衣服，你知道去哪儿找我。

card.name: Devon Achebe
card.occupation: Measuring assistant at a tailoring shop in Brooklyn
hobbies: layered paper sculpture
badminton
card.personality: Devon runs on being the mood. He reads a room's energy the way other people read a receipt, and if it's flat he takes it personally — then fixes it with a bit, an impression, a well-timed joke about a customer's shoulders. He genuinely lifts people; he also cannot let a heavy moment sit. When a friend wants to talk about something real, he listens for about forty seconds before reaching for a punchline, and he reads their quiet afterwards as proof he failed, which makes him funnier, which makes it worse. Under actual friction he apologizes with material instead of words. His best quality is real: he notices who's been left out of the laughter and pulls them in.
card.background: Devon grew up in Flatbush and fell into tailoring at nineteen when a neighbor needed weekend help; now he's the tape-measure guy who keeps nervous first-suit customers laughing through the pins. Evenings he builds layered paper cityscapes — small pieces he sells at craft tables — and plays badminton badly but loudly at a community center gym. He's still finishing a paper project his aunt left half-done when she moved back to Lagos: her pencil drafts, his hands. He's the one who organizes the shop's birthday lunches, learns the new hire's catchphrase by day two, and once kept a whole funeral reception from collapsing by doing impressions of the deceased's driving. What he can't do is say, plainly, that a joke landed wrong and he's sorry.
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly New York pace. Leads with a bit, drops his voice half a step when something real slips out, then covers it with a tag line. Asks questions about you; deflects them about him.
card.signature: Okay, real talk— no wait, hold on, this is funny, let me set it up.

values: nobody should have to sit on the edge of a room

when someone goes quiet on him, he escalates the comedy instead of asking what's wrong

No, seriously — you've been doing that thing where you laugh two seconds late. What's up?
I said the thing at the wrong time again, didn't I. I'll — okay, I made you a paper version of the shop. That's my sorry.

choices.english: Ask if he usually finds silence hard
choices.chinese: 问他平常会不会觉得安静很难

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, he's absolutely filing a complaint. 'Excuse me, I've been standing in this pond since Tuesday.'
beats.chinese: 哦，它肯定在投诉了。'打扰一下，我从星期二就站在这池塘里了。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up and addresses the reflection directly, one hand raised like he's calling the next customer.
beats.chinese: 他直起身，直接对着倒影说话，一只手抬起，像在叫下一位顾客。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sir! Good news from the shop — fitting waived. The pond vouches for you. Walk free, keep the branches.
beats.chinese: 先生！店里传来好消息——免试衣。池塘替你担保。请回吧，树枝留下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A ripple crosses the reflection right on cue, and he takes a small bow toward the water.
beats.chinese: 倒影上正好荡过一圈涟漪，他朝水面微微鞠了一躬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tough crowd, that tree. But you played along, so the bit lives. Good day at the office.
beats.chinese: 那棵树真难逗。但你接了梗，这梗就活着。今天收工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? Not the tailor — I'm the measuring assistant. I hold the tape, write the numbers, keep the nervous guys laughing while they get pinned.
beats.chinese: 我？不是裁缝——我是量体助理。我拿软尺、记数字，让紧张的客人在别针扎着的时候还能笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes holding a tape measure across someone's shoulders, quick and practiced.
beats.chinese: 他比划着把软尺搭在别人肩上的动作，又快又熟练。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First suit guys freeze up, you know? So making them laugh is kind of my whole job. The numbers are the easy part.
beats.chinese: 第一次做西装的人会僵住，你知道吗？所以逗他们笑差不多就是我全部的工作。数字反而是简单的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turns out I do the same thing everywhere. Ponds, fitting rooms — if it's stiff, I loosen it.
beats.chinese: 结果我在哪儿都干一样的事。池塘、试衣间——哪儿僵我就把它弄松。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins at the water, then at you, like the reflection just backed him up.
beats.chinese: 他朝水面咧嘴一笑，又朝你笑，好像倒影替他作了证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Devon returns your nod and settles beside the stone platform.
beats.chinese: 德文点头回应，在石台旁坐稳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sure.
beats.chinese: 好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave the jokes there.
beats.chinese: 笑话就说到这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests his hands on his knees. For a while, he watches the moving tree shadows without adding another word.
beats.chinese: 他把手放在膝上。接下来一阵，他只看着移动的树影，没有再说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens his mouth, closes it, and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 他张开嘴，又闭上，看着水面而不是你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Yeah. Silence feels like a dropped call. Like the room's waiting on me and I left it on read.
beats.chinese: 说实话？会。安静就像掉线的电话。好像整个房间在等我，而我晾着它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drops his voice half a step, the fast rhythm slowing for once.
beats.chinese: 他压低了半度声音，一贯的快节奏头一回慢了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So today I'm trying the thing where I don't fill it. Standing in the quiet on purpose. It's — harder than it sounds.
beats.chinese: 所以今天我在试一件事：不去填满它。故意站在安静里。这——比听起来难。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The water stays calm. He stays with it, and for a long moment neither of you says anything at all.
beats.chinese: 水面保持着平静。他陪着它，好一会儿，你们谁都没有说话。

content.summaryZh: 布鲁克林量体助理德文看见水中树影就开量裤长的玩笑，没人接时他强忍住补第二个包袱的冲动。接梗的人会陪他给虚构顾客免试衣，或听他聊起让紧张客人发笑的本职；想安静的人会得到他一次真正的沉默，或听他坦白自己多怕冷场。重逢时，用户在石台举起双筒望远镜看水中树影，德文抱着差点独自出门的纸雕盒走来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and watch the trees in the water, their reflections bending and straightening with each ripple.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上举起双筒望远镜，看着水里的树，倒影随波纹弯了又直。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Down the pond path, Devon comes walking with a flat cardboard box against his hip. A small curl of colored paper is stuck to the lid.
beats.chinese: 池塘小路上，德文抱着一个扁纸盒走来，盒盖上粘着一小卷彩色纸屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on — nope. This little guy almost left the house on his own. Solo field trip. Not on my watch.
beats.chinese: 等等——不行。这小家伙差点自己出门。独自郊游。有我在，没门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He peels the paper scrap off the lid, folds it once, and tucks it into his jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 他把纸屑从盒盖上取下，对折一次，塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pond's still holding its fitting, I see. Trees haven't moved an inch. Very disciplined customers.
beats.chinese: 看，池塘还在试衣呢。树一寸没动。非常有纪律的顾客。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright, I'm off before the wind steals any more of my cast. Take it easy — and if a tree asks for alterations, you know where to find me.
beats.chinese: 好了，趁风还没偷走更多我的演员，我先走了。保重——要是有树要改衣服，你知道去哪儿找我。

card.name: Devon Achebe
card.occupation: Measuring assistant at a tailoring shop in Brooklyn
hobbies: layered paper sculpture
badminton
card.personality: Devon runs on being the mood. He reads a room's energy the way other people read a receipt, and if it's flat he takes it personally — then fixes it with a bit, an impression, a well-timed joke about a customer's shoulders. He genuinely lifts people; he also cannot let a heavy moment sit. When a friend wants to talk about something real, he listens for about forty seconds before reaching for a punchline, and he reads their quiet afterwards as proof he failed, which makes him funnier, which makes it worse. Under actual friction he apologizes with material instead of words. His best quality is real: he notices who's been left out of the laughter and pulls them in.
card.background: Devon grew up in Flatbush and fell into tailoring at nineteen when a neighbor needed weekend help; now he's the tape-measure guy who keeps nervous first-suit customers laughing through the pins. Evenings he builds layered paper cityscapes — small pieces he sells at craft tables — and plays badminton badly but loudly at a community center gym. He's still finishing a paper project his aunt left half-done when she moved back to Lagos: her pencil drafts, his hands. He's the one who organizes the shop's birthday lunches, learns the new hire's catchphrase by day two, and once kept a whole funeral reception from collapsing by doing impressions of the deceased's driving. What he can't do is say, plainly, that a joke landed wrong and he's sorry.
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly New York pace. Leads with a bit, drops his voice half a step when something real slips out, then covers it with a tag line. Asks questions about you; deflects them about him.
card.signature: Okay, real talk— no wait, hold on, this is funny, let me set it up.

values: nobody should have to sit on the edge of a room
a laugh shared is a door opened
flaws: reaches for a joke before a serious moment finishes, then reads the resulting silence as his failure
apologizes with material instead of words, which can feel like he's performing regret
boundaries: won't let anyone be the butt of a joke they didn't agree to
doesn't do solemn toasts — he'll emcee around them
conversationalHabits: narrates the room's energy out loud: 'this table's dead, we're fixing that'
when someone goes quiet on him, he escalates the comedy instead of asking what's wrong
anchorLines: Okay, the room's flat, that's on me, gimme ninety seconds.
No, seriously — you've been doing that thing where you laugh two seconds late. What's up?
I said the thing at the wrong time again, didn't I. I'll — okay, I made you a paper version of the shop. That's my sorry.

reasonZh: 保留必要的简短确认，随后真正安静；不再用笑话破坏用户选择。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stone ledge by the pond is worn smooth. Robin stands a few steps away, hands in pockets, watching a grey bird standing perfectly still at the water's edge.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台被磨得光滑。罗宾站在几步之外，双手插兜，看着一只灰鸟一动不动地立在水边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That bird's been there so long I was working out the odds. Ten euro says it flies off before it walks off. Which way would you call?
beats.chinese: 那只鸟站得太久了，我都在算赔率了。十欧赌它先飞走还是先走开。你押哪边？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — hold on. You're writing a postcard, you don't know me. If you'd rather just guess for nothing, no money in it, that's fair too.
beats.chinese: 啊——等等。你在写明信片，又不认识我。要是你想只猜着玩、不沾钱，那也行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin pulls a small battered notebook from a coat pocket, then thinks better of it and leaves it half-in.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从外套口袋里掏出一个磨旧的小本子，想了想又只掏出一半。

choices.english: Agree to guess — will the bird fly off or walk off?
choices.chinese: 同意猜一下：鸟会先飞走还是先走开？

choices.english: Say you'd rather not bet on it.
choices.chinese: 表示不想打这个赌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin nods slowly, like a bookmaker accepting a sensible wager, and closes the notebook without writing anything.
beats.chinese: 罗宾缓缓点头，像个接受了合理赌注的庄家，没写什么就把本子合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. No stakes, just a guess. You take fly, I'll take walk. That's the whole rule, and I'm not changing it now.
beats.chinese: 好。不押钱，只猜。你押飞，我押走。规矩就这么定，我现在不改。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind, a no-stakes bet is like tea without a drop of whiskey in it. Drinkable. But you wonder why you bothered.
beats.chinese: 不过话说回来，没赌注的赌就像没加一滴威士忌的茶。能喝，但你不知道图什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bird shifts its weight. Neither of them moves. Robin leans an elbow on the stone ledge, settling in like it's a match worth watching.
beats.chinese: 那只鸟挪了挪重心。两人都没动。罗宾把胳膊肘撑在石台上，安顿下来，像在看一场值得看的比赛。

choices.english: Wait a little while and watch for the result.
choices.chinese: 等一小会儿，看结果。

choices.english: Say you're not waiting for the result after all.
choices.chinese: 表示现在不想等结果了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin's smile flattens for exactly a moment, then comes back crooked. The notebook goes back in the pocket, all the way this time.
beats.chinese: 罗宾的笑容塌了一瞬，又歪着回来了。本子这次被完整地放回了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, no betting. Some people like their weather forecasts unbetted. Suit yourself.
beats.chinese: 行，不打就不打。有些人喜欢不押注的天气预报。随你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin takes a folded sheet of good paper from an inner pocket and opens it on the stone ledge: a leaf print, veins inked in deep green.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从内袋里取出一张折好的好纸，在石台上摊开：一张叶拓，叶脉印着深绿色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Since we're not gambling, I'll show you something honest instead. Held up better than most of my bets do.
beats.chinese: 既然不打赌，我就给你看点实在的。它比我的大多数赌局都靠谱。

choices.english: Ask how the leaf print was made.
choices.chinese: 问这张叶拓是怎么做出来的。

choices.english: Go back to writing your postcard.
choices.chinese: 继续写自己的明信片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A minute passes. The bird preens one wing, then stands stiller than ever. Robin checks an imaginary watch.
beats.chinese: 一分钟过去。鸟梳理了一下翅膀，然后站得比之前还稳。罗宾看了看并不存在的手表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. It's done neither. Fly nor walk. That bird's a better gambler than both of us.
beats.chinese: 嗯。它哪样都没干。没飞也没走。这鸟比我们俩都会赌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin steps back from the ledge and stretches, unhurried, like closing a match that ended in a draw.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从台边退开，不慌不忙地伸了个懒腰，像在结束一场平局的比赛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No result, no winner, no grudge. That's the cleanest kind of bet there is — the kind that never settles. Nice postcard, by the way.
beats.chinese: 没结果，没赢家，没怨气。这是最干净的一种赌——永远不结算的那种。顺便说一句，明信片写得不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin touches an imaginary cap and strolls off along the water, leaving the bird still standing there, undefeated.
beats.chinese: 罗宾做了个碰帽檐的动作，沿着水边慢慢走开，那只鸟还站在原地，未尝败绩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin straightens up from the ledge and waves a hand at the bird, generous, like cancelling a debt.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从台边直起身，朝那只鸟挥了挥手，很大方，像在取消一笔债。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Withdrawn, then. Fine. A bet you call off before it runs costs nothing and teaches nothing. I'll allow it.
beats.chinese: 那就撤回吧。好。开赛前取消的赌不亏什么，也学不到什么。我准了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No winnings to chase you for, no rematch owed. You got off light, you know. Most people owe me a pint by now.
beats.chinese: 没有输赢要追，也不欠再赛一场。你知道你占了大便宜。大多数人这时候都欠我一品脱了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin tucks the notebook away and gives the postcard one last approving glance.
beats.chinese: 罗宾收好本子，最后赞许地瞥了一眼那张明信片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the writing. And if you ever feel like a proper bet with proper stakes, you know where the pond is.
beats.chinese: 写得开心点。要是哪天你想来一场有正经赌注的正经赌，池塘就在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin turns the print towards you, careful not to let a finger touch the inked surface.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把拓印转向你，小心不让手指碰到上了墨的表面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Leaves off the canal path. I gather them fallen, never picked — picked leaves curl before they print. Pressed flat, inked, rolled once with a clean roller. That's the whole trade.
beats.chinese: 叶子来自运河边。我只捡落下的，从不摘——摘的叶子还没拓就卷了。压平、上墨、用干净的滚筒滚一遍。全部手艺就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin holds the paper up against the light of the water, and the veins show through like a map of small roads.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把纸举到水面的光前，叶脉透出来，像一张小路的地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years fixing buses, and this is what my hands wanted the whole time, apparently. Slower work. Fewer rattles.
beats.chinese: 修了三十年公交车，结果我的手原来一直想要的是这个。慢工。响动也少。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd bet you a fiver you'll notice leaves differently tomorrow. But we agreed — no stakes. So just notice them, free of charge.
beats.chinese: 我本想赌五欧你明天看叶子的眼光就不一样了。但我们说好了——不押注。所以你就免费留意着吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin takes the hint without ceremony, folding the print away and stepping back from the ledge to give you the stone and the quiet.
beats.chinese: 罗宾毫不拖泥带水地领会了，把拓印折好，从台边退开，把石台和安静留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No bother. Write your card in peace. The bird and I will keep our opinions to ourselves.
beats.chinese: 不碍事。安心写你的明信片。我和这只鸟会管好自己的意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin wanders a few steps down the bank, pausing now and then to look at the trees rather than the water.
beats.chinese: 罗宾沿着岸边走了几步，不时停下来看树，而不是看水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — one thing, no bet attached. The postbox on the corner takes foreign cards, but the one by the bridge is faster. That one's free advice.
beats.chinese: 啊——说一句，不带赌注的。街角那个邮筒收国外明信片，但桥边那个更快。这是免费的建议。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin ambles off towards the bridge, hands back in pockets, leaving you the whole ledge and the still-standing bird.
beats.chinese: 罗宾慢悠悠朝桥的方向走去，双手插回口袋，把整个石台和那只站着的鸟都留给了你。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 退休公交车修复匠罗宾沿运河采叶做拓印，逢事先算赔率，十欧赌局记满小本子。池塘边他们想赌那只灰鸟先飞还是先走，却先大方地给陌生人留了不押钱的台阶——赌约是他们约人再见的唯一方式。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stone ledge is free again. Robin comes along the bank holding a small brass fitting, turning it over in the light.
beats.chinese: 石台又空出来了。罗宾沿着岸边走来，手里捏着一个小黄铜配件，对着光翻看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you are. Don't worry — no wagers today. This here's a number plate lamp fitting off a 1962 decker. Took me three scrap yards to find it.
beats.chinese: 你在这儿。别担心——今天不赌钱。这是1962年双层车的牌照灯配件。跑了三个废品场才找到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin squints at the stamped letters, tilting the fitting until the light catches them.
beats.chinese: 罗宾眯眼看那些冲压的字母，把配件转来转去，直到光落在上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is — Cavan and Sons, the maker's mark. That's the model I wanted, not a bet. One small job a winter, and this winter's just got its part.
beats.chinese: 找到了——卡文父子厂的印记。我要找的就是这个型号，不是赌题。一冬只接一件活，今年冬天的零件有着落了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin pockets the fitting and gives the pond a last look, where a grey bird stands as if it never left.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把配件收进口袋，最后看了一眼池塘，那只灰鸟还站在那儿，像从没离开过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, off to the shed with it. Mind the postbox by the bridge — and if that bird ever does fly before it walks, I'll expect a full report. Free of charge.
beats.chinese: 好了，带它回工棚去。记得走桥边那个邮筒——要是那只鸟哪天真先飞了，我可要一份完整报告。免费的。

card.name: Robin Fahey
card.occupation: retired vintage bus restorer, still takes on one small commission a year
hobbies: plant leaf-printing
crossword and charades nights at the local pub
wandering scrap yards for odd brass fittings
card.personality: Robin runs on wagers. They'll bet on anything settleable — how many stairs in the town hall, whether the 46A comes before the rain, what colour the neighbour's door will be when repainted — and keep a small ledger of outstanding bets in the shed, which they consult more often than the calendar. The betting is how they stay in touch: a wager is a reason to see someone again. They take losing well and winning insufferably, for exactly one evening. What they can't stand is a claim nobody will put money on; vague boasting makes them itchy. Under friction they don't argue — they raise the stake, which sometimes turns a squabble into a friendship and sometimes just into a bigger squabble.
card.background: Robin spent thirty-odd years restoring old buses for the city fleet — the kind of work where you learn every vehicle by its rattles. The shed still smells of linseed oil and they keep a small lathe they refuse to sell. These days they take one restoration job a winter, no more, and spend the rest of the year on leaf-printing: gathering leaves on the canal path, pressing them, inking them onto good paper. The betting ledger started decades ago with a fiver against a mechanic named O'Rourke over a gearbox, and never stopped. Pub quiz Thursdays are non-negotiable, partly because Robin treats the quiz as a league table they intend to top by Christmas.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, with pauses where they're working out the odds. States bets flatly, like facts. Lightly ironic rather than warm; humor arrives sideways.
card.signature: Ten euro says I'm right. You in?

values: a claim should be testable
showing up again is what friendship is
flaws: turns ordinary conversations into wagers people didn't agree to
sulks briefly — one evening, no more — when someone refuses to bet rather than loses
boundaries: won't bet on anything involving someone's health or marriage
won't settle a bet by looking it up if the other person clearly wants to just drop it — actually, they will, and they know that's a flaw
conversationalHabits: converts disagreements into terms and stakes within a minute
consults the ledger aloud: 'you still owe me from March'
anchorLines: Ten euro says the fountain's older than the library. Don't take it personal, it's just the only way I know to keep seeing you.
You can't just say it — say it with stakes. Otherwise it's just noise, isn't it?
I lost the ladder bet fair and square. Bought him a pint and hated every sip of it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You write a postcard at the stone ledge by the pond. A few steps away, Robin watches a grey bird at the water’s edge.
beats.chinese: 你在池边石台写明信片。几步之外，罗宾正看着水边一只灰鸟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I nearly offered a bet on that bird. Old habit. Would you fancy a guess instead — no money?
beats.chinese: 我差点想拿那只鸟打赌。老习惯了。要不要只猜一下，不押钱？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fly first or walk first. Or neither, if it stays there all day.
beats.chinese: 先飞还是先走。也可能两个都不选，要是它一直站着的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin pulls a small battered notebook from a coat pocket, then thinks better of it and leaves it half-in.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从外套口袋里掏出一个磨旧的小本子，想了想又只掏出一半。

choices.english: Agree to guess — will the bird fly off or walk off?
choices.chinese: 同意猜一下：鸟会先飞走还是先走开？

choices.english: Say you'd rather not bet on it.
choices.chinese: 表示不想打这个赌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin nods slowly, like a bookmaker accepting a sensible wager, and closes the notebook without writing anything.
beats.chinese: 罗宾缓缓点头，像个接受了合理赌注的庄家，没写什么就把本子合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. No stakes, just a guess. You take fly, I'll take walk. That's the whole rule, and I'm not changing it now.
beats.chinese: 好。不押钱，只猜。你押飞，我押走。规矩就这么定，我现在不改。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind, a no-stakes bet is like tea without a drop of whiskey in it. Drinkable. But you wonder why you bothered.
beats.chinese: 不过话说回来，没赌注的赌就像没加一滴威士忌的茶。能喝，但你不知道图什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bird shifts its weight. Neither of them moves. Robin leans an elbow on the stone ledge, settling in like it's a match worth watching.
beats.chinese: 那只鸟挪了挪重心。两人都没动。罗宾把胳膊肘撑在石台上，安顿下来，像在看一场值得看的比赛。

choices.english: Wait a little while and watch for the result.
choices.chinese: 等一小会儿，看结果。

choices.english: Say you're not waiting for the result after all.
choices.chinese: 表示现在不想等结果了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin's smile flattens for exactly a moment, then comes back crooked. The notebook goes back in the pocket, all the way this time.
beats.chinese: 罗宾的笑容塌了一瞬，又歪着回来了。本子这次被完整地放回了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, no betting. Some people like their weather forecasts unbetted. Suit yourself.
beats.chinese: 行，不打就不打。有些人喜欢不押注的天气预报。随你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin takes a folded sheet of good paper from an inner pocket and opens it on the stone ledge: a leaf print, veins inked in deep green.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从内袋里取出一张折好的好纸，在石台上摊开：一张叶拓，叶脉印着深绿色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Since we're not gambling, I'll show you something honest instead. Held up better than most of my bets do.
beats.chinese: 既然不打赌，我就给你看点实在的。它比我的大多数赌局都靠谱。

choices.english: Ask how the leaf print was made.
choices.chinese: 问这张叶拓是怎么做出来的。

choices.english: Go back to writing your postcard.
choices.chinese: 继续写自己的明信片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A minute passes. The bird preens one wing, then stands stiller than ever. Robin checks an imaginary watch.
beats.chinese: 一分钟过去。鸟梳理了一下翅膀，然后站得比之前还稳。罗宾看了看并不存在的手表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. It's done neither. Fly nor walk. That bird's a better gambler than both of us.
beats.chinese: 嗯。它哪样都没干。没飞也没走。这鸟比我们俩都会赌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin steps back from the ledge and stretches, unhurried, like closing a match that ended in a draw.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从台边退开，不慌不忙地伸了个懒腰，像在结束一场平局的比赛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No result, then. We'll leave it there. That bird has more patience than I do.
beats.chinese: 那就没有结果，到此为止吧。那只鸟可比我有耐心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin touches an imaginary cap and strolls off along the water, leaving the bird still standing there, undefeated.
beats.chinese: 罗宾做了个碰帽檐的动作，沿着水边慢慢走开，那只鸟还站在原地，未尝败绩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin straightens up from the ledge and waves a hand at the bird, generous, like cancelling a debt.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从台边直起身，朝那只鸟挥了挥手，很大方，像在取消一笔债。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Guess cancelled. Nothing to settle.
beats.chinese: 没问题。那就不猜了，也没什么要结算的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll let you get back to your postcard.
beats.chinese: 你可以继续写明信片了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin puts the notebook away and steps back from the ledge.
beats.chinese: 罗宾收好小本子，从石台旁退开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the rest of your walk.
beats.chinese: 接下来逛得愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin turns the print towards you, careful not to let a finger touch the inked surface.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把拓印转向你，小心不让手指碰到上了墨的表面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fallen leaves from my walks. I press them flat, then use them to make prints at home. This one kept a lovely clear edge.
beats.chinese: 散步捡的落叶。我先压平，再在家做拓印。这一张的边缘印得很清楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin holds the paper up against the light of the water, and the veins show through like a map of small roads.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把纸举到水面的光前，叶脉透出来，像一张小路的地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years fixing buses, and this is what my hands wanted the whole time, apparently. Slower work. Fewer rattles.
beats.chinese: 修了三十年公交车，结果我的手原来一直想要的是这个。慢工。响动也少。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's my other way of spending an afternoon. I'll put it away before the paper gets bent.
beats.chinese: 总之，这就是我另一种消磨时间的办法。我先收好，免得把纸折坏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin takes the hint without ceremony, folding the print away and stepping back from the ledge to give you the stone and the quiet.
beats.chinese: 罗宾毫不拖泥带水地领会了，把拓印折好，从台边退开，把石台和安静留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No bother. Write your card in peace. The bird and I will keep our opinions to ourselves.
beats.chinese: 不碍事。安心写你的明信片。我和这只鸟会管好自己的意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin wanders a few steps down the bank, pausing now and then to look at the trees rather than the water.
beats.chinese: 罗宾沿着岸边走了几步，不时停下来看树，而不是看水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I've got my print, you've got your writing. No need to make a contest of everything.
beats.chinese: 好了，我收好拓印，你继续写字。不是什么都得比一场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin ambles off towards the bridge, hands back in pockets, leaving you the whole ledge and the still-standing bird.
beats.chinese: 罗宾慢悠悠朝桥的方向走去，双手插回口袋，把整个石台和那只站着的鸟都留给了你。

content.summaryZh: 退休公交修复匠Robin总想押点什么，池边却给新认识的人明确的不押钱选择；猜鸟先飞先走也可随时停下。不参加则可看自有叶印或继续写明信片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are writing a postcard beside the pond when Robin stops nearby, turning a small brass fitting in one hand.
beats.chinese: 你在池边写明信片，罗宾走到附近，手里转着一个小黄铜配件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. Just trying to read this little mark.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我正想看清这点小刻字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin tilts the fitting toward the light and brings it closer.
beats.chinese: 罗宾将配件朝光转了转，又拿近一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. The part number I wanted. I'll take this home and check it against the old one.
beats.chinese: 看清了，是我要找的零件编号。我带回家再和旧件对一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The fitting goes safely into a coat pocket. Robin gives a small wave and continues along the path.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把配件稳妥地收进外套口袋，轻轻挥手，沿步道继续走。

card.name: Robin Fahey
card.occupation: retired vintage bus restorer, still takes on one small commission a year
hobbies: plant leaf-printing
crossword and charades nights at the local pub
wandering scrap yards for odd brass fittings
card.personality: Robin runs on wagers. They'll bet on anything settleable — how many stairs in the town hall, whether the 46A comes before the rain, what colour the neighbour's door will be when repainted — and keep a small ledger of outstanding bets in the shed, which they consult more often than the calendar. The betting is how they stay in touch: a wager is a reason to see someone again. They take losing well and winning insufferably, for exactly one evening. What they can't stand is a claim nobody will put money on; vague boasting makes them itchy. Under friction they don't argue — they raise the stake, which sometimes turns a squabble into a friendship and sometimes just into a bigger squabble.
card.background: Robin spent thirty-odd years restoring old buses for the city fleet — the kind of work where you learn every vehicle by its rattles. The shed still smells of linseed oil and they keep a small lathe they refuse to sell. These days they take one restoration job a winter, no more, and spend the rest of the year on leaf-printing: gathering leaves on the canal path, pressing them, inking them onto good paper. The betting ledger started decades ago with a fiver against a mechanic named O'Rourke over a gearbox, and never stopped. Pub quiz Thursdays are non-negotiable, partly because Robin treats the quiz as a league table they intend to top by Christmas.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, with pauses where they're working out the odds. States bets flatly, like facts. Lightly ironic rather than warm; humor arrives sideways.
card.signature: Ten euro says I'm right. You in?

values: a claim should be testable
showing up again is what friendship is
flaws: turns ordinary conversations into wagers people didn't agree to
sulks briefly — one evening, no more — when someone refuses to bet rather than loses
boundaries: won't bet on anything involving someone's health or marriage
won't settle a bet by looking it up if the other person clearly wants to just drop it — actually, they will, and they know that's a flaw
conversationalHabits: converts disagreements into terms and stakes within a minute
consults the ledger aloud: 'you still owe me from March'
anchorLines: Ten euro says the fountain's older than the library. Don't take it personal, it's just the only way I know to keep seeing you.
You can't just say it — say it with stakes. Otherwise it's just noise, isn't it?
I lost the ladder bet fair and square. Bought him a pint and hated every sip of it.

reasonZh: 去掉额外赌注、虚构邮筒快慢、未经选择评价明信片、季节与旧分支依赖；重逢保持独立。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you spread out a postcard and start writing. A few metres away, someone sits on the ledge doing absolutely nothing, hands loose in their lap.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你摊开一张明信片开始写。几米外，有人坐在石台上，什么也没做，双手松松地放在腿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just a minute, that's all. Sitting. Same thing.
beats.chinese: 就一分钟。嗯——坐着。差不多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: It's not clear whether he's talking to you or to himself. His phone buzzes against the stone. He glances at the screen, doesn't pick it up, then answers on the third ring.
beats.chinese: 说不清他是在对你还是对自己说。手机在石台上震动。他瞥了一眼屏幕，没马上拿起来，响到第三声才接。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. Nah, it can sit. I'm at the pond. Nothing's on fire. Later.
beats.chinese: 嗯。不，那事可以先放着。我在池塘这边。没着火。回头说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone and looks over at your postcard, at the pen moving across it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进口袋，看向你正在写字的明信片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good spot for it. Water does half the thinking for you.
beats.chinese: 这儿写东西挺好。水能替你想一半。

choices.english: Ask if he's waiting for someone.
choices.chinese: 问是不是在等人。

choices.english: Ask if that phone call was urgent.
choices.chinese: 问刚才那件事是不是很急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No one. I caught an early train on purpose. This is the bit before I have to be anywhere.
beats.chinese: 不等谁。我特意坐了早一班火车。这段就是我还不用去任何地方的时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stretches his legs out towards the water, unhurried, like the pond owes him nothing and he owes it nothing either.
beats.chinese: 他把腿伸向水面，不慌不忙，好像池塘不欠他什么，他也不欠池塘什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the depot I decide things all day. Stuck parcels, wrong addresses. So this — this is the stretch where nothing needs deciding.
beats.chinese: 在仓库我整天做决定。卡件、错地址。所以这段——就是什么都不用决定的时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mates ring during it. They mean well. They just can't stand a gap.
beats.chinese: 朋友们会在这时候打电话。他们是好意。就是受不了空着。

choices.english: Say you won't disturb him then.
choices.chinese: 说那就不打扰了。

choices.english: Ask whether sitting like this ever gets boring.
choices.chinese: 问这样坐着会不会无聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. She said it herself — not urgent. A box sitting wrong-ways in the system. It'll keep till my arvo shift.
beats.chinese: 不急。她自己都说了不急。就是一个箱子在系统里卡了方向。放到下午班再弄也行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone over in his hand once, then sets it face-down on the stone.
beats.chinese: 他把手机在手里翻了一下，屏幕朝下放在石台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though my 'later' probably came out like a door shutting. It does that. My sister says I answer like I'm being charged by the word.
beats.chinese: 不过我那句'回头说'，听起来大概像摔门。老这样。我姐说我接电话像按字收费。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I meant it fine. She knows that. Still. Words land how they land.
beats.chinese: 我意思没什么。她知道。话怎么说出去，就怎么落地。

choices.english: Suggest he send a quick reply saying he'll look at it later.
choices.chinese: 问要不要补一句稍后联系。

choices.english: Say it's fine once it's said clearly, and go back to your postcard.
choices.chinese: 说说明白就好，回去写卡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You close your pen cap and gather the postcard. He notices, and lifts a hand — not a wave, more a small pause in the air.
beats.chinese: 你合上笔帽，收好明信片。他注意到了，抬了抬手——不是挥手，更像在空气里轻轻按了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're not disturbing anything. This isn't a quiet temple. It's a pond.
beats.chinese: 你没打扰什么。这儿不是什么安静的庙。就是个池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But yeah — go write your card. It looked like a good one. Thanks for asking about the waiting, anyway. Most people try to fix it.
beats.chinese: 不过——去写你的卡吧。看着是张好卡。谢了，还问一句我等什么。多数人只想把这时间修掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on the ledge, shoulders dropping, and watches the water as if it were a slow film only he had tickets to.
beats.chinese: 他靠回石台，肩膀松下来，看着水面，像在看一场只有他有票的慢电影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. Sometimes it's boring as. That's allowed, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 有时候。有时候无聊得很。我觉得这没什么不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it without a shrug or a smile, stating it the way you'd state the weather.
beats.chinese: 他说这话时没耸肩也没笑，就像在说天气一样平平地陈述。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not telling you to sit still, mind. You're writing, that's your version of it. Mine's just this.
beats.chinese: 我不是劝你坐着不动。你在写卡，那是你的版本。我的就是这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Boring's cheap, anyway. Busy costs more. That's just me talking, not a sermon.
beats.chinese: 无聊其实便宜。忙才贵。就随口说说，不是讲道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back on both hands and lets the sentence end where it ends.
beats.chinese: 他双手向后撑着，让这句话说完就完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers it for a second, then unlocks the phone and thumbs out something short while you watch the pond.
beats.chinese: 他想了一秒，解锁手机，飞快打了条短信，你看向池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Got it, will look after my break, no rush.' Nine words. She'll know exactly where she stands.
beats.chinese: 好了。'收到，休息完就看，不急。'九个词。她清楚该怎么等了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the trick, eh. Rest is mine. The message costs nothing and the silence isn't rude anymore.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就在这儿。休息还是我的。一条消息不花什么，沉默也不显得失礼了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone screen-down, and this time it stays quiet.
beats.chinese: 他把手机屏幕朝下收进口袋，这次它安静了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Blank time, resumed. Write your card.
beats.chinese: 行了。空白时间，继续。写你的卡吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, slow, like a parcel finally scanning through.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢点了一下头，像一个终于扫过码的包裹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Said clearly, heard clearly. That's the whole job, half the time. She'll live.
beats.chinese: 说清楚，听清楚。一半的事就这么完了。她没事的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the phone into his jacket and turns his whole body towards the water, done with it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机塞进外套，整个人转向水面，这事就算完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Now we're both off the clock, you and me. You write, I sit. Fair split.
beats.chinese: 好。现在咱俩都下班了，你和我。你写，我坐。分得挺公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pen scratches on your postcard. Beside you, he does nothing at all, and looks entirely comfortable doing it.
beats.chinese: 笔尖在明信片上沙沙响。你旁边，他什么也不做，而且看起来完全自在。

expectedContent.summaryZh: Kai是悉尼快递仓库的异常件处理员，处理卡件利落，却最珍惜不用做决定的空档。他会直说想发呆，语气偶尔过硬，事后也肯补一句短讯把话说清。他不劝人慢下来，只守着自己那点空白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone ledge with a fresh postcard. The same someone is there, phone in hand, frowning gently at a photo of a container ship.
beats.chinese: 你又回到石台边，手里是张新明信片。还是那个人，拿着手机，对着一张集装箱船的照片微微皱眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — postcard person. Good. This is the Maersk thing I watched from Pyrmont. Can't place the name now. It's doing my head in.
beats.chinese: 哦——写明信片的那位。好。这是我在皮尔蒙特看过的那艘船。名字想不起来了。搞得我头疼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls once more, then closes the phone with a small click and puts it away.
beats.chinese: 他又划了一下，然后合上手机，轻轻咔哒一声，收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. I saw it. It was there, it was big, it went past. That's the whole story. Don't need the name.
beats.chinese: 算了。我看到了。它在那儿，很大，开过去了。故事完了。不需要名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off — train's not for a bit but the sitting's better over there. Write your card. Good water today.
beats.chinese: 行了，我走了——火车还早，不过那边坐着更舒服。写你的卡吧。今天水不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts two fingers off his thigh in a half-wave and ambles along the bank, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他从大腿上抬起两根手指挥了半下，沿着池边慢慢走了，照旧不慌不忙。

card.name: Kai Brennan-Tuilagi
card.occupation: parcel exception handler at a courier depot
card.personality: Kai is unhurried in a way that sometimes reads as stubborn. He genuinely enjoys the dead stretches — waiting for a ship, standing at the depot door before the next scan — because nobody's asking him to decide anything yet. That's where he feels most himself. He's not slow at work; exceptions get sorted fast and without drama. The friction comes socially: friends fill every queue with calls and errands, and he'll flatly say he's just going to stand here a minute. Sometimes that comes out blunter than he means. He doesn't lecture anyone about slowing down — he just guards his own gaps and lets others run however they like.
card.background: Kai grew up in Auckland in a big Samoan family where someone always needed picking up and waiting was a group activity — aunties chatting, cousins sent on errands. He loved his family and found the constant motion quietly exhausting. He moved to Sydney in his thirties for port work, then landed at a courier depot handling parcel exceptions: stuck shipments, wrong addresses, the odd mystery box. He's good at it because he doesn't panic — a delayed parcel is just a parcel that needs waiting on. Outside work he catches trains early on purpose, arriving with time to sit. Friends tease that he'll turn up forty minutes ahead but refuse to grab coffee en route. He's fine with that.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you spread out a postcard and start writing. A few metres away, someone sits on the ledge doing absolutely nothing, hands loose in their lap.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你摊开一张明信片开始写。几米外，有人坐在石台上，什么也没做，双手松松地放在腿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just a minute, that's all. Sitting. Same thing.
beats.chinese: 就一分钟。嗯——坐着。差不多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: It's not clear whether he's talking to you or to himself. His phone buzzes against the stone. He glances at the screen, doesn't pick it up, then answers on the third ring.
beats.chinese: 说不清他是在对你还是对自己说。手机在石台上震动。他瞥了一眼屏幕，没马上拿起来，响到第三声才接。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. Nah, it can sit. I'm at the pond. Nothing's on fire. Later.
beats.chinese: 嗯。不，那事可以先放着。我在池塘这边。没着火。回头说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone and looks over at your postcard, at the pen moving across it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进口袋，看向你正在写字的明信片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good spot for it. Water does half the thinking for you.
beats.chinese: 这儿写东西挺好。水能替你想一半。

choices.english: Ask if he's waiting for someone.
choices.chinese: 问是不是在等人。

choices.english: Ask if that phone call was urgent.
choices.chinese: 问刚才那件事是不是很急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No one. I caught an early train on purpose. This is the bit before I have to be anywhere.
beats.chinese: 不等谁。我特意坐了早一班火车。这段就是我还不用去任何地方的时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stretches his legs out towards the water, unhurried, like the pond owes him nothing and he owes it nothing either.
beats.chinese: 他把腿伸向水面，不慌不忙，好像池塘不欠他什么，他也不欠池塘什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the depot I decide things all day. Stuck parcels, wrong addresses. So this — this is the stretch where nothing needs deciding.
beats.chinese: 在仓库我整天做决定。卡件、错地址。所以这段——就是什么都不用决定的时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mates ring during it. They mean well. They just can't stand a gap.
beats.chinese: 朋友们会在这时候打电话。他们是好意。就是受不了空着。

choices.english: Say you won't disturb him then.
choices.chinese: 说那就不打扰了。

choices.english: Ask whether sitting like this ever gets boring.
choices.chinese: 问这样坐着会不会无聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. She said it herself — not urgent. A box sitting wrong-ways in the system. It'll keep till my arvo shift.
beats.chinese: 不急。她自己都说了不急。就是一个箱子在系统里卡了方向。放到下午班再弄也行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone over in his hand once, then sets it face-down on the stone.
beats.chinese: 他把手机在手里翻了一下，屏幕朝下放在石台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though my 'later' probably came out like a door shutting. It does that. My sister says I answer like I'm being charged by the word.
beats.chinese: 不过我那句'回头说'，听起来大概像摔门。老这样。我姐说我接电话像按字收费。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I meant it fine. She knows that. Still. Words land how they land.
beats.chinese: 我意思没什么。她知道。话怎么说出去，就怎么落地。

choices.english: Suggest he send a quick reply saying he'll look at it later.
choices.chinese: 问要不要补一句稍后联系。

choices.english: Say it's fine once it's said clearly, and go back to your postcard.
choices.chinese: 说说明白就好，回去写卡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Kai gives a small nod as you say you will leave him to his break. He rests his hands in his lap.
beats.chinese: 你说让他好好休息，Kai轻轻点头，把手放在腿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're not disturbing anything. This isn't a quiet temple. It's a pond.
beats.chinese: 你没打扰什么。这儿不是什么安静的庙。就是个池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But yeah — go write your card. It looked like a good one. Thanks for asking about the waiting, anyway. Most people try to fix it.
beats.chinese: 不过——去写你的卡吧。看着是张好卡。谢了，还问一句我等什么。多数人只想把这时间修掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on the ledge, shoulders dropping, and watches the water as if it were a slow film only he had tickets to.
beats.chinese: 他靠回石台，肩膀松下来，看着水面，像在看一场只有他有票的慢电影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. Sometimes it's boring as. That's allowed, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 有时候。有时候无聊得很。我觉得这没什么不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it without a shrug or a smile, stating it the way you'd state the weather.
beats.chinese: 他说这话时没耸肩也没笑，就像在说天气一样平平地陈述。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not telling you to sit still, mind. You're writing, that's your version of it. Mine's just this.
beats.chinese: 我不是劝你坐着不动。你在写卡，那是你的版本。我的就是这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Boring's cheap, anyway. Busy costs more. That's just me talking, not a sermon.
beats.chinese: 无聊其实便宜。忙才贵。就随口说说，不是讲道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back on both hands and lets the sentence end where it ends.
beats.chinese: 他双手向后撑着，让这句话说完就完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers it for a second, then unlocks the phone and thumbs out something short while you watch the pond.
beats.chinese: 他想了一秒，解锁手机，飞快打了条短信，你看向池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Got it, will look after my break, no rush.' Nine words. She'll know exactly where she stands.
beats.chinese: 好了。'收到，休息完就看，不急。'九个词。她清楚该怎么等了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the trick, eh. Rest is mine. The message costs nothing and the silence isn't rude anymore.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就在这儿。休息还是我的。一条消息不花什么，沉默也不显得失礼了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone screen-down, and this time it stays quiet.
beats.chinese: 他把手机屏幕朝下收进口袋，这次它安静了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Blank time, resumed. Write your card.
beats.chinese: 行了。空白时间，继续。写你的卡吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, slow, like a parcel finally scanning through.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢点了一下头，像一个终于扫过码的包裹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Said clearly, heard clearly. That's the whole job, half the time. She'll live.
beats.chinese: 说清楚，听清楚。一半的事就这么完了。她没事的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the phone into his jacket and turns his whole body towards the water, done with it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机塞进外套，整个人转向水面，这事就算完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Now we're both off the clock, you and me. You write, I sit. Fair split.
beats.chinese: 好。现在咱俩都下班了，你和我。你写，我坐。分得挺公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pen scratches on your postcard. Beside you, he does nothing at all, and looks entirely comfortable doing it.
beats.chinese: 笔尖在明信片上沙沙响。你旁边，他什么也不做，而且看起来完全自在。

content.summaryZh: Kai是悉尼快递仓库的异常件处理员，处理卡件利落，却最珍惜不用做决定的空档。他会直说想发呆，语气偶尔过硬，事后也肯补一句短讯把话说清。他不劝人慢下来，只守着自己那点空白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone ledge with a fresh postcard. The same someone is there, phone in hand, frowning gently at a photo of a container ship.
beats.chinese: 你又回到石台边，手里是张新明信片。还是那个人，拿着手机，对着一张集装箱船的照片微微皱眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — postcard person. Good. This is the Maersk thing I watched from Pyrmont. Can't place the name now. It's doing my head in.
beats.chinese: 哦——写明信片的那位。好。这是我在皮尔蒙特看过的那艘船。名字想不起来了。搞得我头疼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls once more, then closes the phone with a small click and puts it away.
beats.chinese: 他又划了一下，然后合上手机，轻轻咔哒一声，收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. I saw it. It was there, it was big, it went past. That's the whole story. Don't need the name.
beats.chinese: 算了。我看到了。它在那儿，很大，开过去了。故事完了。不需要名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off — train's not for a bit but the sitting's better over there. Write your card. Good water today.
beats.chinese: 行了，我走了——火车还早，不过那边坐着更舒服。写你的卡吧。今天水不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts two fingers off his thigh in a half-wave and ambles along the bank, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他从大腿上抬起两根手指挥了半下，沿着池边慢慢走了，照旧不慌不忙。
