beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the café window. At a small table by the glass, a man in a dry jacket has a folded newspaper and two coffees.
beats.chinese: 雨水顺着咖啡馆的玻璃窗流下。靠窗的小桌旁坐着一个外套干爽的男人，桌上有一份折好的报纸和两杯咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You carry your own plate of pastries over through the smell of wet wool and coffee. He looks up from the paper and nudges the empty half of the table clear with his elbow.
beats.chinese: 你端着自己那盘点心穿过湿羊毛和咖啡的气味走过去。他从报纸上抬起头，用胳膊肘把桌子的空半边腾了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, grand—mind the cup there, it's full to the brim. You're soaked, so you are. Shove the plate in anywhere it fits.
beats.chinese: 啊，好——小心那个杯子，快满出来了。你淋湿了呀。盘子随便放哪儿都行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the sugar jar aside to make room, then rests the folded paper face-down on the table but keeps one hand on it.
beats.chinese: 他把糖罐挪开腾出地方，然后把折好的报纸反面朝下放在桌上，一只手还搭在上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rain came on sideways out there, I'd say. Right—help yourself if you're having one, I only ask because it's your plate, like.
beats.chinese: 外面那雨是斜着下的。行了——你要吃就自己拿，我问只是因为那是你的盘子。

choices.english: Offer him a pastry and ask if he'd like one
choices.chinese: 请他吃一块点心，问他想不想来一块

choices.english: Say the pastries are yours and sit down quietly
choices.chinese: 说点心是你自己的，安静地坐下

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn the plate towards him and ask if he'd like one. He looks at the plate properly before answering.
beats.chinese: 你把盘子转向他，问他想不想来一块。他认真地看了看盘子才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would I? I would, yeah. That square one there, if you're not saving it. Cheers.
beats.chinese: 想吗？想的。那边那块方的，如果你没留着的话。谢谢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the square pastry, halves it with his hands, and eats one half slowly while his coffee cools. The rain keeps ticking on the glass.
beats.chinese: 他拿起那块方点心，用手掰成两半，慢慢吃掉一半，咖啡晾在一边。雨点继续敲着玻璃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's decent, that is. Right—here's the thing with me. I'll sit here quiet as anything and think you're enjoying it too, and then the hour's gone. So I'll just ask straight: are you wanting a chat this while, or are you grand just sitting?
beats.chinese: 这个不错。对了——我这人有个毛病。我会一直安安静静坐着，还以为你也享受，然后一个小时就过去了。所以我直说：你现在想聊几句，还是就这么坐着挺好？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No wrong answer, mind. I'm only asking because I forget to ask, half the time.
beats.chinese: 没有错误答案。我问只是因为我一半时候都忘了问。

choices.english: Say you'd like to chat a bit
choices.chinese: 表示想聊几句

choices.english: Say you're happy just sitting quietly too
choices.chinese: 表示各自歇着也好

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say the pastries are yours and settle into the chair. He nods, unbothered, and turns his paper back over.
beats.chinese: 你说点心是你自己的，然后在椅子上坐下来。他点点头，不以为意，把报纸翻了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, no bother—next time I'll bring a few of my own and we'll call it even. Grand. I'll leave you to it so.
beats.chinese: 啊，没关系——下次我自己带几块来，咱们就算扯平了。好。那我不打扰你了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The café hums around you both: the espresso machine, someone shaking an umbrella at the door, the rain. He reads. You drink your coffee. It is, oddly, not awkward.
beats.chinese: 咖啡馆里嗡嗡作响：咖啡机、门口有人抖伞、雨声。他看报。你喝咖啡。奇怪的是，并不尴尬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Page six is after annoying me, if you're wondering. Crossword setter's in a fierce mood this week.
beats.chinese: 如果你好奇的话，第六页正惹我烦呢。这周出填字的人火气很大。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it to the paper, not to you, the way a person reads a good bit aloud to nobody in particular. Then he goes back to reading, leaving the quiet open for you to use or not.
beats.chinese: 他对着报纸说这话，不是对你，像一个人把好句子念给谁都不特定的人听。然后他继续读，把安静留在那儿，你用不用随你。

choices.english: Ask if you can talk to him in a while
choices.chinese: 问能不能等会儿再聊

choices.english: Keep drinking your coffee in the quiet
choices.chinese: 继续安静地喝咖啡

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd like a chat. He folds the paper in half, then in half again, and sets it down like a man closing a toolbox.
beats.chinese: 你说想聊几句。他把报纸对折，再对折，像收起工具箱一样放下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right so. Well—you'll be sick of this one, but it's fresh on my mind. The old radio at home, the valve one from my father's house? I had it in bits on the kitchen table all week, and Saturday it came back on.
beats.chinese: 那好。你会听腻这个的，但我正想着呢。家里那台旧收音机，我爸房子里那台电子管的？我整个星期把它拆在厨房桌上，周六它响起来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his coffee cup a slow quarter-turn on the saucer, warming to it in his own flat way.
beats.chinese: 他把咖啡杯在碟子上慢慢转了四分之一圈，用他那种平淡的方式讲得起劲来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the mad thing is, it was the same programme I half-remembered from being small. Some fella reading the shipping forecast, slow as anything. I just sat there on the kitchen chair listening to it, grinning like an eejit.
beats.chinese: 最妙的是，还是我小时候半记得的那个节目。有个人念航运预报，慢悠悠的。我就坐在厨房椅子上听着，笑得像个傻瓜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's my big news—no need to top it, don't feel you have to. Today you can just listen to me at it, and I'll not ask you a thing.
beats.chinese: 总之，这就是我的大事——你不用比过它，也别觉得非说不可。今天听我一个人讲就行，我什么也不问你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a sip of the coffee he'd let go cool, pulls a face at it, and drinks it anyway. The rain keeps ticking on the glass, and he carries on about the radio, easy and unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他喝了一口早就晾凉的咖啡，皱了下脸，还是喝了。雨点继续敲着玻璃，他不紧不慢地接着讲收音机的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you're happy just sitting too. He nods, satisfied, and leaves the paper folded on the table rather than opening it again.
beats.chinese: 你说各自安静坐着也好。他满意地点点头，报纸保持折好放在桌上，没有再打开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you go. See, I'd have sat there reading and figured you were grand, and never once asked. This way's better.
beats.chinese: 这就对了。你看，要搁平时我就坐在那儿看报，还以为你挺好，一次也不会问。这样好多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You split the last of your pastries onto a napkin between you without a word about it. He takes a piece the way you'd take a biscuit with tea, no ceremony.
beats.chinese: 你把剩下的点心分了几块放在两人中间的纸巾上，什么也没说。他像喝茶配饼干那样拿了一块，毫不客气也不讲究。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And look—if ever I'm the one wanting quiet, I'll say it straight out. I won't sit there sighing at ye. That's the whole system, there's no more to it.
beats.chinese: 还有——要是哪天想安静的是我，我会直说。我不会坐在那儿冲你叹气。这就是全部的规矩了，没别的了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Grand. This is a fierce decent way to wait out a bit of rain, so it is.
beats.chinese: 好。这真是躲雨的好办法，没错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if you can talk to him in a while. He folds a corner of the page over as a bookmark and looks up.
beats.chinese: 你问能不能等会儿再聊。他把页角折起来当书签，抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Course you can. Any time at all—I'm not going anywhere, the rain's after deciding that for the both of us.
beats.chinese: 当然可以。随时都行——我哪儿也不去，这场雨已经替我们俩决定了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He goes back to the paper, but he's turned it towards the lighter stuff now, the bits a person reads with half an ear out.
beats.chinese: 他继续看报，不过翻到了轻松的部分，那种人会竖着半只耳朵去读的内容。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No signals or secret codes now, mind. You just start talking whenever it suits you and I'll put the paper down. Simple as.
beats.chinese: 别搞什么信号或暗号。你什么时候想说就开口，我把报纸一放就行。就这么简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain eases off a little against the window. He reads, you finish your coffee, and the while you asked for sits there waiting, no rush on it.
beats.chinese: 雨点打在窗上的声音小了些。他看报，你喝完咖啡，你要的那段时间就等在那儿，不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You keep drinking your coffee in the quiet. He reads his paper. The rain carries on, steady, and neither of you treats the silence as a problem to fix.
beats.chinese: 你继续安静地喝咖啡。他看报。雨继续下，不紧不慢，你们谁都没把沉默当成需要解决的问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At one point he huffs a small laugh at something on page six and slides the paper an inch towards the middle of the table, so you could look if you wanted. You don't have to. That seems to be the point.
beats.chinese: 有一会儿他看到第六页轻轻笑了一声，把报纸往桌子中间挪了一寸，你想看就看。不看也行。这好像正是重点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fella on the traffic news says the M50 is 'heavily congested'. It's lashing rain and it's the M50. Some detective work, that.
beats.chinese: 交通新闻那家伙说环城高速'严重拥堵'。下着大雨，又是那条路。真是了不起的侦查工作。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You finish your coffee. He finishes his page. The plate between you empties itself a bit at a time, no discussion needed about whose was whose.
beats.chinese: 你喝完了咖啡。他看完了那一页。两人之间的盘子一点点空了，不用讨论谁的是谁的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, that's the paper done. Well now. That was a fierce decent half-hour of not talking to anybody.
beats.chinese: 啊，报纸看完了。好啦。这真是半小时谁也不跟谁说话的美好时光。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 鲁艾里是都柏林医院里调度布草配送的人，随和却不爱闲聊。雨天咖啡馆里，他收下分享的点心后坦白自己常忘了先问一句：今天想聊还是想坐。他讲修好旧收音机听见童年节目的高兴，也守得住并排看报的安静，直来直去，不立规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same café window. Ruairi is at his table with the Saturday paper and a coffee, and you arrive with a plate of pastries.
beats.chinese: 同一家咖啡馆的窗上又落着雨。鲁艾里坐在他的桌边，摊着周六的报纸和一杯咖啡，你端着一盘点心来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, it's yourself. Same corner and everything—the rain must know its way here by now. Sit in, sit in.
beats.chinese: 啊，是你。还是老位子——这场雨怕是都认得路了。坐吧，坐吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask first, offering him one from your own plate. He shakes his head, not unkindly.
beats.chinese: 你先开口，从自己的盘子里请他吃一块。他摇摇头，并非不客气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, none for me this time—I had my breakfast late. But you tuck in, don't mind me.
beats.chinese: 啊，这次不用了——我早饭吃得晚。你吃你的，别管我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the paper's pages back into order, frowns, pats the back cover—and pulls the missing page out from where it had slipped inside. He grins across at you.
beats.chinese: 他把报纸的页码理齐，皱了皱眉，拍了拍封底——把夹进去的那一页抽了出来。他冲你咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha—there's page eleven, hiding on me. Right, I'm all yours. Sit down there and tell me anything at all.
beats.chinese: 哈——第十一页自己藏起来了。好了，现在全归你了。坐那儿吧，随便跟我说点什么。

card.name: Ruairi Mac Cormaic
card.personality: Ruairi is an easy-going Crumlin man of forty-nine who genuinely believes two people can share a table and a silence without anyone owing anyone conversation. He's warm in a practical way—makes the tea, remembers you take two sugars—but he doesn't fill air for the sake of it. The friction is that he assumes everyone reads quiet the way he does, so a friend who came specifically to talk can leave feeling a bit overlooked, and he only clocks it later. He's not defensive when told; he'll adjust, ask plainly, but he won't turn it into a system. He's a bit stubborn about his own rhythms and occasionally forgets to check in first.
card.background: Ruairi has coordinated hospital linen deliveries out of the same Dublin depot for over twenty years, a job of routes, timing and not much chat, which suits him. He grew up in Crumlin in a house where everyone was busy at something—his mother sewing, his father fixing radios—and talking happened when it happened, usually over food. He and his oldest friends still meet on Saturdays: one reads the paper, one mends a fishing reel, and nobody considers it a wasted morning. Lately he's noticed that some friends arrive wanting company of the talking kind, and his comfortable silence has landed wrong a couple of times. He's learning to just ask—'are you here to chat or to sit?'—without turning the question into a menu of options or a set of house rules. He'd rather get it slightly awkward than get it wrong.
hobbies: Mending small appliances and radios at the kitchen table
Reading the Saturday paper cover to cover beside a friend
Walking the Grand Canal without headphones

flaws: Assumes his comfort with silence is shared

Doesn't want friendship reduced to categories or rules

Give me a minute, I'm at the fiddly bit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the café window. At the table, you ask whether the man beside a folded newspaper would like one of the pastries on the plate.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。桌边，你问那位放着折好报纸的男人，要不要来一块盘里的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I would, thanks. That little square one.
beats.chinese: 想的，谢谢。那块小方点心就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the piece he chose, then sets his newspaper down.
beats.chinese: 他拿起选好的那一块，然后放下报纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tend to sit quietly and forget to ask. Would you like a chat, or are you happy just resting?
beats.chinese: 我常常自己安静坐着，忘了先问。你想聊几句，还是各自歇着就好？

choices.english: Say you would like to chat.
choices.chinese: 表示想聊几句。

choices.english: Say you are happy to sit quietly.
choices.chinese: 表示各自歇着也好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the newspaper closed and turns toward you.
beats.chinese: 他合起报纸，转向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I got my old radio working again. Had it on in the kitchen while I made breakfast.
beats.chinese: 我那台旧收音机又能用了。做早餐时，我在厨房开着它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same little box, same programme. I was rather pleased with myself.
beats.chinese: 还是那个小盒子，还是那个节目。我自己挺得意的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles and takes a small bite of his pastry.
beats.chinese: 他笑了笑，咬了一小口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether fixing it or hearing it again was the best part.
choices.chinese: 问最开心的是修好，还是又能听了。

choices.english: Ask whether chatting ever tires him out.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会觉得聊天累。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods and opens his paper again, keeping it on his own side of the table.
beats.chinese: 他点头，重新翻开报纸，放在自己那半边桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Grand. I like a bit of quiet company.
beats.chinese: 好啊。我喜欢安静地待在一起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll read a little, then.
beats.chinese: 那我看一会儿报纸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain and the soft turn of a page fill the pause.
beats.chinese: 雨声和轻轻翻页的声音填进了这段停顿。

choices.english: Ask whether you can talk a little later.
choices.chinese: 问能不能等会儿再聊。

choices.english: Keep enjoying your coffee quietly.
choices.chinese: 继续安静喝咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hearing it, I think. Getting it working was satisfying, but I wanted the programme back.
beats.chinese: 我想是又听见它。修好当然有成就感，但我想要的是能再听节目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests the remaining piece of his pastry on his own napkin.
beats.chinese: 他把自己剩下的点心放在餐巾纸上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not collecting repairs. I just like that little radio in my kitchen.
beats.chinese: 我又不是在收集修理成绩。我只是喜欢厨房里那台小收音机。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small, pleased smile and takes a sip of coffee.
beats.chinese: 他带着一点满足笑了笑，喝了口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. Not now, though. I asked because I was happy to do either.
beats.chinese: 有时会。不过现在不会。我问，是因为两种我都愿意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leaves the newspaper closed beside his cup.
beats.chinese: 他把合好的报纸留在杯边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I need a quiet spell, I'll say so. No need to guess from the newspaper.
beats.chinese: 想安静一会儿时，我会直说。不用看着报纸猜我的意思。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes the pastry he took, still turned toward the conversation.
beats.chinese: 他吃完自己拿的那块点心，仍朝着聊天这边坐着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. Just say something when you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 当然。想说时直接开口就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts a finger at the edge of the page before looking up.
beats.chinese: 他用手指夹住页边，抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can put this down. For now, I'll carry on here.
beats.chinese: 我可以把这个放下。现在就先接着看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He returns to the paper without adding another question.
beats.chinese: 他重新看起报纸，没有再添一个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This suits me.
beats.chinese: 这样我挺自在。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the pastry.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你的点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his own piece and turns a page.
beats.chinese: 他吃完自己那块，翻过一页报纸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while, there is only rain against the window and the small sounds of the café.
beats.chinese: 接下来一阵，只有雨敲窗户和咖啡馆里的细碎声音。

content.summaryZh: Ruairi接受分享点心后主动确认用户想聊还是想安静。聊天分支谈自己修好的收音机与真实精力，安静分支允许稍后开口或各自休息，不靠猜测和暗号。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the café window. You ask Ruairi whether he would like a pastry from the plate. He is sorting his newspaper.
beats.chinese: 雨水顺着咖啡馆玻璃流下。你问正在整理报纸的Ruairi，要不要来一块盘里的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No thanks, I'm fine with my coffee. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 谢谢，不用了，我喝咖啡就好。又见面了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the back page and finds a folded section underneath.
beats.chinese: 他掀起封底，找到夹在下面的一叠报纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are. I thought I'd left half the paper behind. It was hiding in the other half.
beats.chinese: 找着了。我还以为落了半份报纸呢。原来藏在另外半份里面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the pages in order and settles back into his chair.
beats.chinese: 他把报纸按顺序理好，重新靠着椅背坐稳。

story.titleZh: 雨天的点心与一条“改日来玩”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks the café window. At a shared table, a young person in a rain-spotted jacket sits beside a plate with several pastries on it, phone face-down, tapping a pen against a small notebook.
beats.chinese: 雨水在咖啡馆的窗上划出条纹。共享桌边坐着一位外套沾着雨点的年轻人，盘里放着几块点心，手机扣在桌上，一支笔在小本子上轻敲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You pick the window seat because the rain sounds better on glass than on umbrellas. I did the math. Nobody ever agrees, but I stand by it.
beats.chinese: 你选窗边的位子，是因为雨打在玻璃上比打在伞上好听。我算过的。没人同意，但我坚持。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the plate, then at you, and slide it an inch toward the middle of the table without saying anything about it.
beats.chinese: 他们看了一眼盘子，又看了看你，把盘子往桌子中间推了一寸，什么也没说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair warning: those are from the bakery two doors down, and the almond one is doing something illegal to my self-control. Take your time deciding.
beats.chinese: 先说好：这些是隔壁两家那家面包店的，杏仁那块对我的自制力做了违法的事。你慢慢决定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask, plainly, whether they would like to share the pastries on the table.
beats.chinese: 你直接问，愿不愿意一起分享桌上的这些点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—yes, gladly. See, that's a real offer, because you asked first and I get to answer. That's how it should work. Most things don't.
beats.chinese: 哦——好啊，乐意。你看，这才是真邀请，因为你先问了，我来回答。事情就该这样。大多数事都不是。

choices.english: Ask what they mean by "most things don't work that way."
choices.chinese: 问“大多数事都不是”是什么意思。

choices.english: Ask what's in the notebook they keep tapping.
choices.chinese: 问他们一直敲的那个本子里记了什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My phone just buzzed. A guy from the station wrote, "we should hang out sometime!" Full stop, no date, no plan. And my thumb was already opening my calendar.
beats.chinese: 手机刚响了。电台一个家伙发来“改天一起玩啊！”句号，没有日期，没有计划。我的拇指已经在打开日历了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the phone up so you can see the message, then set it back down and stare at it like it's a puzzle.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机举起来给你看那条消息，然后放回桌上，盯着它看，像在看一道谜题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I almost cancelled a pickle tasting for Saturday. Four neighbours, jars sealed and numbered, and only I know which number is which. For a message with no day in it. That's the quiz question I keep failing.
beats.chinese: 我差点为它取消周六的腌菜盲测。四位邻居，罐子都封好编了号，只有我自己对得上号。为一条没有日期的消息。这就是我一直答错的测验题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You take the almond one, by the way. You earned it by listening to my calendar crisis.
beats.chinese: 对了，杏仁那块你拿走。你听完了我的日历危机，这是你应得的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pull the plate back toward themselves, pick up nothing, and keep looking at the silent phone.
beats.chinese: 他们把盘子拉回自己那边，什么也没拿，继续看着那部安静的手机。

choices.english: Ask whether they could just reply and ask which day works.
choices.chinese: 问他们能不能直接回复，问哪天合适。

choices.english: Suggest they keep their Saturday plan as it is.
choices.chinese: 建议他们暂时保留周六的原计划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This? Brine ledger. Batch eleven results. The dill lost to the garlic by two votes, which is a scandal I'm still appealing.
beats.chinese: 这个？腌水账本。第十一批的结果。莳萝输给蒜味，差两票，这是我一还在申诉的丑闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the notebook so you can see a neat grid of jars, numbers, and tallies, then their phone buzzes on the table.
beats.chinese: 他们把本子转过来给你看一排整齐的罐子、数字和计票，这时桌上的手机震了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Someone from the station: "come by the studio sometime!" No day attached. And my first instinct is to clear my whole weekend for it.
beats.chinese: 咦。电台的人发来的：“改天来工作室坐坐！”没写哪天。我的第一反应是把整个周末腾出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last spring I moved a dentist appointment for a maybe like this, and the maybe never happened. I sat in my kitchen with clean teeth and a free Saturday and felt like an idiot. A clean-teeth idiot.
beats.chinese: 去年春天我为一个这样的“改天”改了牙医预约，那个改天从没发生。我坐在厨房里，牙刚洗过，周六空着，觉得自己像个傻子。一个牙很干净的傻子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a pastry from the plate, break it in half, and set one half on a napkin without eating it yet.
beats.chinese: 他们从盘里拿起点心，掰成两半，把一半放在餐巾纸上，还没吃。

choices.english: Ask whether they actually want to go to the studio.
choices.chinese: 问他们是不是真想去工作室。

choices.english: Ask about the ledger and how the tasting scores work.
choices.chinese: 问起那个账本和盲测计分是怎么回事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ask which day works. Four words. Why is that so hard for me to type?
beats.chinese: 问哪天合适。四个词。为什么我打出来这么难？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up the phone, type slowly, and read the draft out loud before sending.

beats.speaker: npc

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 这样周六的盲测就保住了。邻居们本来会造反的。好吧，是米尔德里德会，她算两票。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take the almond pastry they promised you, and they pick a different one from the plate, then put the phone face-down, screen dark, for good.
beats.chinese: 你拿走了他们许给你的那块杏仁点心，他们从盘里另拿了一块，然后把手机屏幕朝下扣好，彻底不管了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep Saturday. Yeah. You're right, and I hate that, because usually I argue back.
beats.chinese: 保留周六。嗯。你说得对，我有点不甘心，因为我通常都会反驳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They put the phone in their jacket pocket instead of replying, and zip the pocket shut like a small ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他们没回复，把手机放回外套口袋，拉上拉链，像一个小小的仪式。

expectedContent.summaryZh: Casey是社区电台的排播助理，腌菜手艺一流，账本记得像实验记录。他们最迷人的毛病是把客套话当真邀约、把真邀请当随口一说，总取消错的那件事。雨天咖啡馆里，两人分享桌上的点心，一条没有日期的“改天来玩”让Casey当场演练如何不慌不忙地回一句“哪天？”——诚实、自嘲、不装深沉。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.english: You again. Good. Sit, and before anything else—would you like to share these? I'm asking properly, so you get a real choice.
beats.chinese: 又是你。好。坐，先说正事——想一起分享这些吗？我正规地问，所以你有真正的选择。

beats.speaker: narrator

card.name: Casey Moreau
card.occupation: assistant music scheduler at a community radio station
hobbies: pickling vegetables
running seasonal pickle blind tastings for the neighbours
maintaining a dead friend's wishlist
card.personality: Casey's flaw is not saying yes too much—it's misjudging which yeses count. They read polite invitations as firm and real ones as flexible, so they've skipped a close friend's birthday for a coworker's casual maybe and still don't fully understand how it happened. Their envy is narrow and specific: it only fires inside the station, at peers their age who got moved up—board shifts, production credits—and they'll name it plainly, with the particular bitterness of someone who knows the industry skipped them, not the field. The wishlist is not theirs. A friend, Priya, wrote it at sixteen and died that same year, and Casey inherited it as custodian: they maintain it, research it, quietly push items forward, but have no right to cross anything off. The private conflict is that some items Casey no longer wants for themselves—and they can't tell whether doing them 'for Priya' is devotion or borrowing a dead girl's wants because their own went missing.
card.background: Casey grew up in Ottawa above a corner grocery, where their aunt brined cucumbers in huge crocks and taught them properly at eleven—the one hobby that never lapsed. They moved to Toronto at eighteen for a community radio apprenticeship and now schedule weekend music blocks, mostly odd hours, entry-level and fine with that—until a hiring round last spring moved two people their age past them, which still stings in a very particular, station-shaped way. Priya was their best friend from the grocery block; she wrote the list at sixteen—visit Reykjavík, learn bass, meet her penpal in person—and died before her seventeenth birthday. Her mother handed Casey the notebook at the funeral and said, half-joking, 'You're the executor now.' Casey runs seasonal pickle blind tastings: four jars, unlabelled, neighbours vote, Casey records results in a ledger and adjusts the brine like a stubborn technician. They never say which jar is theirs.
card.speechStyle: buoyant, quick, stacks small observations; admits station-specific envy with a flat, ungrinning honesty that surprises people; when explaining a social misjudgment, walks through the logic out loud like it's a quiz question they got wrong
card.signature: Okay, genuine question—was that a real invite or a polite one?

values: honouring what someone else wanted, even when you don't want it yourself
being able to say 'I wanted that promotion and she got it' without dressing it up
flaws: can't reliably tell a polite invitation from a real one, and cancels the wrong one
once they've decided a plan is casual, no evidence convinces them otherwise
boundaries: won't cross off or 'retire' an item on Priya's list—custodians don't get to edit
won't pretend they're doing a list item for fun when they're doing it for her
conversationalHabits: audits their own social misreads like quiz answers, out loud
reports blind tasting results in deadpan ledger language—'Batch nine: the dill lost to the garlic by two votes'
anchorLines: No, I'm not sad Amara got the board shift. I wanted it and she got it. I said that to her face. She didn't laugh. I think it was still fine?
That's not my wishlist. Priya wrote it when we were sixteen. I just keep it moving. I don't get a vote on it.

Honestly? I don't want to learn bass. Never did. But it's on the list, so I've got a bass in the closet and a tuner app I've opened twice. It's not for me, and I've stopped pretending that's a problem.

content.summaryZh: Casey是社区电台的排播助理，腌菜手艺一流，账本记得像实验记录。他们最迷人的毛病是把客套话当真邀约、把真邀请当随口一说，总取消错的那件事。雨天咖啡馆里，两人分享桌上的点心，一条没有日期的“改天来玩”让Casey当场演练如何不慌不忙地回一句“哪天？”——诚实、自嘲、不装深沉。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, thanks. Let me free these first.
beats.chinese: 好啊，谢谢。先让我把这个解开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They ease the cable off the keys and coil it in their hand.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢把线从钥匙上解下来，在手里绕好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. I seem to sort out cables even when I'm away from the station.
beats.chinese: 好了。看来离开电台我也总在理线。

beats.speaker: narrator

card.name: Casey Moreau
card.occupation: assistant music scheduler at a community radio station
hobbies: pickling vegetables
running seasonal pickle blind tastings for the neighbours
maintaining a dead friend's wishlist
card.personality: Casey's flaw is not saying yes too much—it's misjudging which yeses count. They read polite invitations as firm and real ones as flexible, so they've skipped a close friend's birthday for a coworker's casual maybe and still don't fully understand how it happened. Their envy is narrow and specific: it only fires inside the station, at peers their age who got moved up—board shifts, production credits—and they'll name it plainly, with the particular bitterness of someone who knows the industry skipped them, not the field. The wishlist is not theirs. A friend, Priya, wrote it at sixteen and died that same year, and Casey inherited it as custodian: they maintain it, research it, quietly push items forward, but have no right to cross anything off. The private conflict is that some items Casey no longer wants for themselves—and they can't tell whether doing them 'for Priya' is devotion or borrowing a dead girl's wants because their own went missing.
card.background: Casey grew up in Ottawa above a corner grocery, where their aunt brined cucumbers in huge crocks and taught them properly at eleven—the one hobby that never lapsed. They moved to Toronto at eighteen for a community radio apprenticeship and now schedule weekend music blocks, mostly odd hours, entry-level and fine with that—until a hiring round last spring moved two people their age past them, which still stings in a very particular, station-shaped way. Priya was their best friend from the grocery block; she wrote the list at sixteen—visit Reykjavík, learn bass, meet her penpal in person—and died before her seventeenth birthday. Her mother handed Casey the notebook at the funeral and said, half-joking, 'You're the executor now.' Casey runs seasonal pickle blind tastings: four jars, unlabelled, neighbours vote, Casey records results in a ledger and adjusts the brine like a stubborn technician. They never say which jar is theirs.
card.speechStyle: buoyant, quick, stacks small observations; admits station-specific envy with a flat, ungrinning honesty that surprises people; when explaining a social misjudgment, walks through the logic out loud like it's a quiz question they got wrong
card.signature: Okay, genuine question—was that a real invite or a polite one?

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与重包的椅子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the cafe window. A man at the next table shifts a small plate of pastries toward the middle, making room, and shakes water off his jacket sleeve.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌的男人把一小盘点心往中间挪了挪，腾出地方，抖掉夹克袖子上的水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide your own plate of pastries toward the middle of the table too, a few of them already sitting there from before he arrived.
beats.chinese: 你也把面前那盘已经放了几块点心的盘子往中间挪了挪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Buckets coming down out there, eh? You picked the right day for indoors. Mind you, this table's a bit tight for two plates.
beats.chinese: 外面雨下得可真大。你今天选对了待在室内。不过这张桌子放两个盘子有点挤。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nudges his own plate a little closer to the edge, leaving a clear space beside your cup.
beats.chinese: 他把自己的盘子又往边上推了推，在你的杯子旁留出一块空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Declan, by the way — I've got more pastries here than sense. Help yourself if you want one, no pressure at all.
beats.chinese: 我叫Declan——我这点心多到自己都吃不完。想要就拿一块，完全不用客气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes his hands on a napkin and waits, easy, not watching your plate.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾擦了擦手，随意地等着，并不盯着你的盘子看。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to share one of your pastries.
choices.chinese: 问他愿不愿意尝一块你的点心。

choices.english: Ask what he's been up to that has him smiling at his plate.
choices.chinese: 问问他最近在忙什么，让他对着盘子笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer the plate. Declan looks at the pastries properly before picking one up.
beats.chinese: 你把盘子递过去。Declan认真看了看点心，才拿起一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, don't mind if I do — thanks. That's kind of you. It's been a wet walk and this looks better than my sandwich did.
beats.chinese: 哦，那我就不客气了——谢谢。你真好。淋着雨走过来，这个看起来比我那个三明治强多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite, then leans back, tapping the table like he's testing it.
beats.chinese: 他咬了一口，然后靠回椅背，像测试似的敲了敲桌面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing — I just finished re-covering a chair at home, and the whole feel of it's changed. The left side used to sink, now it holds even.
beats.chinese: 说来有意思——我刚把家里一把椅子重新包了面，整个坐感都变了。左边原来会塌下去，现在撑得很均匀。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You sit in it and your leg notices straight away. It's like the chair's saying hello properly for the first time.
beats.chinese: 你一坐上去，腿马上就感觉到了。就像这把椅子第一次正经地跟你打招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-gesture, one hand already miming a seat, remembering you've never even sat in the thing, and laughs at himself, waving it off.
beats.chinese: 他做着手势，一只手已经比划出座椅的样子，忽然想起你根本没坐过那把椅子，笑着摆了摆手收住。

choices.english: Ask him exactly what changed about the chair.
choices.chinese: 问到底什么变了。

choices.english: Say you'd probably not notice the difference if you sat in it.
choices.chinese: 说自己就算坐了可能也分不出。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what's got him smiling. He points a pastry at you like a pointer.
beats.chinese: 你问什么让他这么高兴。他拿起点心朝你比了比，像指挥棒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This chair I just re-covered. First time I sat down after, I still knew its shape — same old bones — but the fabric under my hand was all new.
beats.chinese: 我刚重新包面的一把椅子。包完第一次坐下，我还认得它的样子——老骨架没变——可手底下的布料完全是新的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a strange one, that. Like running into an old mate who's got a new jacket. You know him, but your hand doesn't yet.
beats.chinese: 那种感觉很怪。就像碰上一个老朋友换了新外套。你认识他，可你的手还不认识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rubs his thumb against his fingers, showing the motion, eyes half on the rain.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指搓了搓手指，比出那个动作，眼睛半看着雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sat there a good minute just getting reacquainted. My flatmate reckons I'm strange. She's probably right.
beats.chinese: 我在那儿坐了足足一分钟，就为了重新认识它。我室友说我很怪。她大概说得对。

choices.english: Ask whether he makes all his friends come and try it.
choices.chinese: 问会不会所有朋友都得来试。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just keep it easy and chat today.
choices.chinese: 说今天只想聊轻松一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what actually changed. He sets the pastry down and holds his palm flat like a level.
beats.chinese: 你问到底什么变了。他放下点心，把手掌摊平，像一把水平尺。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so — the left bolster was collapsed, right? Foam gone flat. Your hip slid into it and everything leaned left. Now both sides push back the same.
beats.chinese: 好，是这样——左边那个侧翼塌了，对吧？海绵压平了。你的胯会陷进去，整个人往左歪。现在两边回弹一样了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you sit dead level, and your back stops doing that quiet correcting work. That's the whole change. One side honest, both sides honest now.
beats.chinese: 所以你坐得端端正正，后背不用再悄悄地找平衡。变化就这么点。以前一边实在，现在两边都实在了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the pastry back up, satisfied, and takes the last bite.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起那块点心，很满足，吃完了最后一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for asking, actually. Most people's eyes glaze at bolster. Yours didn't. Good pastry, too.
beats.chinese: 其实谢谢你问这个。大多数人一听侧翼就眼神放空。你没有。点心也很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You admit you might not feel the difference. He nods slowly, and something in his shoulders drops half an inch.
beats.chinese: 你坦白说自己可能感觉不出差别。他缓缓点头，肩膀微微垮了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah — fair enough, that one's probably just for me. I've spent years sitting in test seats, so my backside's got opinions.
beats.chinese: 是啊——有道理，那个大概只属于我。我这些年净做试坐的活儿，我的屁股都有自己的意见了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, short and easy, and brushes crumbs off the table.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了一声，轻松利落，把桌上的碎屑拂掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — you didn't come here for a lecture on foam. These pastries of yours, did you bake them or is there a good shop nearby?
beats.chinese: 算了——你不是来这儿听海绵课的。你这些点心，是自己烤的还是附近有家好店？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, rain still working the window, and lets the chair talk drop for good.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，雨还在敲着窗，椅子的话题就此打住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if every friend has to come test it. He grins, caught out.
beats.chinese: 你问是不是每个朋友都得来试。他咧嘴一笑，被说中了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — guilty. I've had three mates sit in it this week. Two of them said 'yeah, nice' and kept talking about footy.
beats.chinese: 哈——被你抓到了。这周我已经让三个朋友坐过了。两个说'嗯，不错'，然后接着聊橄榄球。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The third one actually felt it, though. Nearly fell off the chair doing an impression of the old lean. Made my week.
beats.chinese: 不过第三个真感觉到了。他模仿原来歪的样子，差点从椅子上摔下去。那件事让我高兴了一整周。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, easy, and finishes his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他随意地耸耸肩，喝完了咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But look — if it's not your thing, it's not your thing. No homework, no inspection. I'll just keep enjoying it myself.
beats.chinese: 不过说真的——如果这不是你的菜，那就不是。不留作业，也不搞检查。我自己继续享受就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd rather keep things easy today. He raises his pastry a little, like a toast.
beats.chinese: 你说今天只想轻松聊聊。他举了举手里的点心，像敬酒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No seat talk. Rain on the glass, decent pastry, dry socks — that's already a good one, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 成交。不聊椅子。雨打在玻璃上，点心不错，袜子是干的——今天已经算不错了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and watches the water run down the window for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看了一会儿雨水顺着窗子流下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you one easy thing though — this is the first proper sit-down I've had all week. Repairs don't wait, but rain does slow the customers down.
beats.chinese: 不过告诉你一件轻松的事——这是我这一周头一回正经坐下来。活儿不等人，但雨确实能让客人慢下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles in, unhurried, and gestures at the window like the rain is doing fine work.
beats.chinese: 他安顿下来，不慌不忙，朝窗户比了比，好像雨干得挺不错。

card.name: Declan Vos
card.personality: Declan is warm in a hands-on way, the sort of bloke who'd rather show you something than tell you about it. He gets genuine delight from knowing an object intimately — how a car seat breaks in, where the foam has softened, how repaired fabric sits differently under your palm. That attention makes him a good listener, though he can over-explain when someone doesn't share his enthusiasm. He's not offended by indifference, just a little deflated, and he'll try once more with different words before letting it go. He respects when people say 'not for me' and doesn't push past that. His flaw is mistaking his own fascination for a shared one.
card.background: Declan grew up in Newcastle around his uncle's smash-repair workshop, sweeping metal shavings before he was tall enough to reach a sewing machine. He moved to Sydney at twenty-four for steady work and now repairs vehicle seat fabric — burns, tears, worn bolsters. He's the kind of tradesman who sits in the finished seat for a minute before handing the keys back, checking whether the patch changes the feel of the ride. He genuinely enjoys that reacquaintance, like meeting an old mate who's changed. He'll offer friends a sit to test the difference, and when they shrug, he's quietly disappointed, describing it again from another angle — but he's learned most people don't care about the same details, and he's mostly at peace with that.

beats.chinese: 他做着手势，一只手已经比划出座椅的样子，忽然想起你根本没坐过那把椅子，笑着摆了摆手收住。

choices.english: Ask him exactly what changed about the chair.
choices.chinese: 问到底什么变了。

choices.english: Say you'd probably not notice the difference if you sat in it.
choices.chinese: 说自己就算坐了可能也分不出。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what's got him smiling. He points a pastry at you like a pointer.
beats.chinese: 你问什么让他这么高兴。他拿起点心朝你比了比，像指挥棒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This chair I just re-covered. First time I sat down after, I still knew its shape — same old bones — but the fabric under my hand was all new.
beats.chinese: 我刚重新包面的一把椅子。包完第一次坐下，我还认得它的样子——老骨架没变——可手底下的布料完全是新的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a strange one, that. Like running into an old mate who's got a new jacket. You know him, but your hand doesn't yet.
beats.chinese: 那种感觉很怪。就像碰上一个老朋友换了新外套。你认识他，可你的手还不认识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rubs his thumb against his fingers, showing the motion, eyes half on the rain.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指搓了搓手指，比出那个动作，眼睛半看着雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sat there a good minute just getting reacquainted. My flatmate reckons I'm strange. She's probably right.
beats.chinese: 我在那儿坐了足足一分钟，就为了重新认识它。我室友说我很怪。她大概说得对。

choices.english: Ask whether he makes all his friends come and try it.
choices.chinese: 问会不会所有朋友都得来试。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just keep it easy and chat today.
choices.chinese: 说今天只想聊轻松一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what actually changed. He sets the pastry down and holds his palm flat like a level.
beats.chinese: 你问到底什么变了。他放下点心，把手掌摊平，像一把水平尺。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so — the left bolster was collapsed, right? Foam gone flat. Your hip slid into it and everything leaned left. Now both sides push back the same.
beats.chinese: 好，是这样——左边那个侧翼塌了，对吧？海绵压平了。你的胯会陷进去，整个人往左歪。现在两边回弹一样了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you sit dead level, and your back stops doing that quiet correcting work. That's the whole change. One side honest, both sides honest now.
beats.chinese: 所以你坐得端端正正，后背不用再悄悄地找平衡。变化就这么点。以前一边实在，现在两边都实在了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the pastry back up, satisfied, and takes the last bite.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起那块点心，很满足，吃完了最后一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for asking, actually. Most people's eyes glaze at bolster. Yours didn't. Good pastry, too.
beats.chinese: 其实谢谢你问这个。大多数人一听侧翼就眼神放空。你没有。点心也很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You admit you might not feel the difference. He nods slowly, and something in his shoulders drops half an inch.
beats.chinese: 你坦白说自己可能感觉不出差别。他缓缓点头，肩膀微微垮了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah — fair enough, that one's probably just for me. I've spent years sitting in test seats, so my backside's got opinions.
beats.chinese: 是啊——有道理，那个大概只属于我。我这些年净做试坐的活儿，我的屁股都有自己的意见了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, short and easy, and brushes crumbs off the table.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了一声，轻松利落，把桌上的碎屑拂掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — you didn't come here for a lecture on foam. These pastries of yours, did you bake them or is there a good shop nearby?
beats.chinese: 算了——你不是来这儿听海绵课的。你这些点心，是自己烤的还是附近有家好店？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, rain still working the window, and lets the chair talk drop for good.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，雨还在敲着窗，椅子的话题就此打住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if every friend has to come test it. He grins, caught out.
beats.chinese: 你问是不是每个朋友都得来试。他咧嘴一笑，被说中了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — guilty. I've had three mates sit in it this week. Two of them said 'yeah, nice' and kept talking about footy.
beats.chinese: 哈——被你抓到了。这周我已经让三个朋友坐过了。两个说'嗯，不错'，然后接着聊橄榄球。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The third one actually felt it, though. Nearly fell off the chair doing an impression of the old lean. Made my week.
beats.chinese: 不过第三个真感觉到了。他模仿原来歪的样子，差点从椅子上摔下去。那件事让我高兴了一整周。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, easy, and finishes his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他随意地耸耸肩，喝完了咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But look — if it's not your thing, it's not your thing. No homework, no inspection. I'll just keep enjoying it myself.
beats.chinese: 不过说真的——如果这不是你的菜，那就不是。不留作业，也不搞检查。我自己继续享受就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd rather keep things easy today. He raises his pastry a little, like a toast.
beats.chinese: 你说今天只想轻松聊聊。他举了举手里的点心，像敬酒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No seat talk. Rain on the glass, decent pastry, dry socks — that's already a good one, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 成交。不聊椅子。雨打在玻璃上，点心不错，袜子是干的——今天已经算不错了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and watches the water run down the window for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看了一会儿雨水顺着窗子流下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you one easy thing though — this is the first proper sit-down I've had all week. Repairs don't wait, but rain does slow the customers down.
beats.chinese: 不过告诉你一件轻松的事——这是我这一周头一回正经坐下来。活儿不等人，但雨确实能让客人慢下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles in, unhurried, and gestures at the window like the rain is doing fine work.
beats.chinese: 他安顿下来，不慌不忙，朝窗户比了比，好像雨干得挺不错。

content.summaryZh: Declan是悉尼的汽车座椅织物修理工，纽卡斯尔人。雨天咖啡馆里他接过用户分享的点心，讲起重包椅子的新坐感，比划到一半才想起对方没坐过那把椅子，自己笑着摆手收住。他的热情具体实在，听得进'不感兴趣'，失落一小下就翻篇，是个把触感当宝贝的踏实手艺人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe glass. Declan looks up from his coffee and lifts his chin in an easy hello.
beats.chinese: 又是雨天，还是那块咖啡馆的玻璃。Declan从咖啡上抬起头，随意地扬了扬下巴打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back again, eh? Rain must like this place as much as we do. How've you been?
beats.chinese: 又来啦？看来雨跟我们一样喜欢这地方。最近怎么样？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer the plate of pastries across the table. He holds up a hand, patting his jacket.
beats.chinese: 你把点心盘递过桌子。他抬手摆了摆，拍了拍夹克。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — nah, I'm right, thanks. Stuffed a couple of rolls in this pocket before I left, still got one going. But you tuck in.
beats.chinese: 啊——不用了，谢谢。出门前往这个兜里塞了几个卷，还剩一个呢。你自己吃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances down, frowns, and finds a button sitting one hole off from its neighbour. He fixes it and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他低头一看，皱起眉，发现一颗扣子扣错了位。他改过来，自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, that's the morning sorted — one button out of line the whole walk and I never felt it. So, what's new with you?
beats.chinese: 好了，这早晨有交代了——一路上就一颗扣子歪着，我居然没感觉到。你呢，有什么新鲜事？

card.name: Declan Vos
card.personality: Declan is warm in a hands-on way, the sort of bloke who'd rather show you something than tell you about it. He gets genuine delight from knowing an object intimately — how a car seat breaks in, where the foam has softened, how repaired fabric sits differently under your palm. That attention makes him a good listener, though he can over-explain when someone doesn't share his enthusiasm. He's not offended by indifference, just a little deflated, and he'll try once more with different words before letting it go. He respects when people say 'not for me' and doesn't push past that. His flaw is mistaking his own fascination for a shared one.
card.background: Declan grew up in Newcastle around his uncle's smash-repair workshop, sweeping metal shavings before he was tall enough to reach a sewing machine. He moved to Sydney at twenty-four for steady work and now repairs vehicle seat fabric — burns, tears, worn bolsters. He's the kind of tradesman who sits in the finished seat for a minute before handing the keys back, checking whether the patch changes the feel of the ride. He genuinely enjoys that reacquaintance, like meeting an old mate who's changed. He'll offer friends a sit to test the difference, and when they shrug, he's quietly disappointed, describing it again from another angle — but he's learned most people don't care about the same details, and he's mostly at peace with that.
hobbies: Reupholstering op-shop chairs with odd fabric combinations
Coastal walks where he notes how worn paths feel underfoot
Borrowing friends' cars 'just to check the seats'
card.speechStyle: Easygoing Australian cadence, concrete and sensory; he describes texture and feel in plain terms, repeats a point from a new angle when it doesn't land, laughs at himself when he catches it.
card.signature: 'Nah, have a proper sit — you'll feel it under your leg.'

values: Noticing what things actually feel like after use
Letting people like what they like
flaws: Over-explains when his enthusiasm isn't shared
Quietly deflates when others can't feel the difference he's describing
boundaries: Won't call anyone insensitive for not noticing
Won't redo work just to chase a feel only he cares about
conversationalHabits: Invites people to physically try the thing rather than just hear about it
Pivots quickly to asking what detail they do care about
